sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Choose a template, paper profile, records and copies. Generate a preview, verify the identifying information, then open Print preview. Use actual size and disable browser headers. Save as PDF through the browser print dialog. Printing records a request, not confirmed physical delivery.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: The API rejects invalid records, excessive copies and labels that do not fit the paper. Reprints require permission and a reason. Retry preserves the operation identity. Payment links are synthetic; only an administrator can simulate payment status, and expired requests cannot be printed.

Your default stock does not fit this label. A compatible profile is selected for this preview; your saved default is unchanged. The tenant-locked printer stock does not fit this label. Ask your administrator to unlock it or select compatible stock.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The server isolates jobs by tenant, application and user. Tenant administrators control copy limits, reprints and locked printer profiles. Users can save an unlocked default profile. Screen preferences and language apply to the interface; printed codes retain approved dimensions and black-on-white contrast.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Inject LabelAdapter and effective preferences into LabelPrintingWorkspace. The authenticated POST /label-printing API owns record lookup, code generation and job history. Templates use JSON; synthetic records and scoped jobs use CSV. Replace the adapter for real applications. Payment providers, direct thermal printing and physical scanner certification remain external integrations.

paragraphs: Open Invoices & payments, then View bill for the full invoice, insurance, line totals, receipts and revision history. sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: OP Registration keeps patient selection, registration, care and checkout in one page. Its five-step progress bar, patient strip, contextual side panels and bottom actions stay inside the existing application shell. All patient and encounter data comes from the authenticated demo API.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Search for a patient or create one using New patient. Confirm name and date of birth, review visit details, coverage and consent, then register and check in. Use the Nursing, Consultation, Orders, Billing and Checkout tabs without leaving this page. Sign the note before consultation charges post. Complete services before their charges post. Use the worklist to reopen a saved encounter.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: The server rejects missing identity and consent, duplicate active visits, stale record versions, invalid vital signs and payments above the balance. Signed notes use addenda. Pending results require an owner, due date and plan before checkout. Network retries reuse the operation ID. Saved drafts require identity and consent review again; tenant storage, retention and field exclusions apply. Reloading a conflicting record replaces the local form, so compare your values first.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Navigation access and write permission are checked by the demo API. The demo administrator can write; other authorized users can read. Effective theme, font scales, density, table settings, number/date/time formatting and language are inherited, including tenant locks. Currency comes from the ledger; formatting does not convert amounts. The five-step workflow and care tabs are fixed by this template, rather than the generic record navigation preference.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Compose RegistrationWorkspace with a RegistrationAdapter, ClinicalTemplateAdapter, authenticated scopeKey and PreferenceHost. The POST /op-registration endpoint loads configuration and executes versioned commands. Providers and services are read from CSV; encounters, appointments, payments and retry receipts share an atomic CSV snapshot scoped by tenant and application. Patient demographics reuse the existing patient API. These encounter records are separate from the older consultation and billing template stores. No real payer, payment, messaging or electronic-signature integration is connected.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: This library previews backend-generated barcode and QR labels. Use dedicated pages for items, specimens, patient bands, documents, payment demos, batch printing and printer profiles.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Choose a template, paper profile, records and copies. Generate a preview, verify the identifying information, then open Print preview. Use actual size and disable browser headers. Save as PDF through the browser print dialog. Printing records a request, not confirmed physical delivery.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: The API rejects invalid records, excessive copies and labels that do not fit the paper. Reprints require permission and a reason. Retry preserves the operation identity. Payment links are synthetic; only an administrator can simulate payment status, and expired requests cannot be printed.

Your default stock does not fit this label. A compatible profile is selected for this preview; your saved default is unchanged. The tenant-locked printer stock does not fit this label. Ask your administrator to unlock it or select compatible stock.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The server isolates jobs by tenant, application and user. Tenant administrators control copy limits, reprints and locked printer profiles. Users can save an unlocked default profile. Screen preferences and language apply to the interface; printed codes retain approved dimensions and black-on-white contrast.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Inject LabelAdapter and effective preferences into LabelPrintingWorkspace. The authenticated POST /label-printing API owns record lookup, code generation and job history. Templates use JSON; synthetic records and scoped jobs use CSV. Replace the adapter for real applications. Payment providers, direct thermal printing and physical scanner certification remain external integrations.

After saving, return to the worklist and verify the customer appears with the expected details. If another session changed the record, reload and compare before resubmitting.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Enter at least one search criterion, then select Search. Search anywhere matches whole words, quoted phrases and exclusions; the labelled fields support partial values. More filters includes ID type, nationality, residing country, gender, date of birth and status.

Choose table or cards and open patient details inline, in a dialog, or in a drawer. Previous and next navigate the current result page. Save a named preset to the API, or reuse recent searches kept only in this workspace session. Record, booking, encounter and 360 actions retain patient identity.
Pass a ClinicalTemplateAdapter to ClinicalPatientWorkspace. The demo adapter uses the authenticated clinical-templates endpoint; business data and form metadata come from the API.
Saves validate fields and identity duplicates, enforce record versions and reuse operation IDs for retries. Review the latest record explicitly after a conflict.
The shared shell supplies language, direction, theme, font, density, formatting and form navigation preferences. Preview controls do not change tenant policy.

sections.title: Billing corrections and shared clinical rail
paragraphs: Open Invoices & payments, then View bill for the full invoice, insurance, line totals, receipts and revision history. Edit bill changes quantities, discount, insurance authorization and notes on unpaid issued invoices. Enter a correction reason and confirm. sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Search for a patient or create one using New patient. Confirm name and date of birth, review visit details, coverage and consent, then register and check in. sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: The server rejects missing identity and consent, duplicate active visits, stale record versions, invalid vital signs and payments above the balance. Signed notes use addenda. Pending results require an owner, due date and plan before checkout. Network retries reuse the operation ID. Saved drafts require identity and consent review again; tenant storage, retention and field exclusions apply. Reloading a conflicting record replaces the local form, so compare your values first.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Navigation access and write permission are checked by the demo API. The demo administrator can write; other authorized users can read. Effective theme, font scales, density, table settings, number/date/time formatting and language are inherited, including tenant locks. Currency comes from the ledger; formatting does not convert amounts. The five-step workflow and care tabs are fixed by this template, rather than the generic record navigation preference.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Compose RegistrationWorkspace with a RegistrationAdapter, ClinicalTemplateAdapter, authenticated scopeKey and PreferenceHost. The POST /op-registration endpoint loads configuration and executes versioned commands. Providers and services are read from CSV; encounters, appointments, payments and retry receipts share an atomic CSV snapshot scoped by tenant and application. Patient demographics reuse the existing patient API. These encounter records are separate from the older consultation and billing template stores. No real payer, payment, messaging or electronic-signature integration is connected.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Choose a template, paper profile, records and copies. Generate a preview, verify the identifying information, then open Print preview. Use actual size and disable browser headers. Save as PDF through the browser print dialog. Printing records a request, not confirmed physical delivery.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: The API rejects invalid records, excessive copies and labels that do not fit the paper. Reprints require permission and a reason. Retry preserves the operation identity. Payment links are synthetic; only an administrator can simulate payment status, and expired requests cannot be printed.

Your default stock does not fit this label. A compatible profile is selected for this preview; your saved default is unchanged. The tenant-locked printer stock does not fit this label. Ask your administrator to unlock it or select compatible stock.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The server isolates jobs by tenant, application and user. Tenant administrators control copy limits, reprints and locked printer profiles. Users can save an unlocked default profile. Screen preferences and language apply to the interface; printed codes retain approved dimensions and black-on-white contrast.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Inject LabelAdapter and effective preferences into LabelPrintingWorkspace. The authenticated POST /label-printing API owns record lookup, code generation and job history. Templates use JSON; synthetic records and scoped jobs use CSV. Replace the adapter for real applications. Payment providers, direct thermal printing and physical scanner certification remain external integrations.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Build a reusable frontend template with approved shared controls. This designer saves demo drafts, not published backend DCP forms.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Choose a section and add components from the palette. Drag handles or move buttons reorder items. Select a field to edit its label, required state, section, minimum or dropdown options. Preview uses temporary answers. Save design draft persists the design; Open saved design restores it.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Designs require titles, unique stable IDs and valid dropdown options. Limits are 20 sections, 100 fields and 50 options per field. Failed saves retain edits and retries reuse the operation ID. Conflicts require reopening the latest saved design after reviewing unsaved changes.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Only demo administrators can save designs. Drafts are isolated by tenant, application and user. Shared controls follow effective theme, density, typography and tenant locks. Preview does not save business answers or grant record access.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Inject DesignerAdapter and PreferenceHost into DcpDesignerWorkspace. The demo endpoint stores frontend template drafts in CSV snapshots. Backend DCP conversion, publication, datasets, rules and entity binding require the separate host adapter; no PostgreSQL or Java service is provisioned here.

sections.title: Purpose
paragraphs: Sanitized application diagnostics collected by Sentinel.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Filter incidents by page and status. Open an incident to inspect sanitized diagnostics. Move it to Investigating or Resolved. A recurring failure reopens a resolved incident.

sections.title: Purpose
paragraphs: Find and resume your unfinished work.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Opening never submits a record or approval. Reselect CSV files to restore mappings. Refresh if another window changed a draft. Each application has its own recovery center.
Draft storage is enabled by your tenant policy. Only service-acknowledged changes are recoverable.

paragraphs: Enter at least one search criterion, then select Search. Search anywhere matches whole words, quoted phrases and exclusions; the labelled fields support partial values. More filters includes ID type, nationality, residing country, gender, date of birth and status.

sections.title: Billing corrections and shared clinical rail
paragraphs: Open Invoices & payments, then View bill for the full invoice, insurance, line totals, receipts and revision history. Edit bill changes quantities, discount, insurance authorization and notes on unpaid issued invoices. Enter a correction reason and confirm. The API recalculates using its current tariffs and retains the previous invoice snapshot. Payment history, including refunds, prevents edits. Conflicts require loading and reviewing the latest ledger before saving again. Unsaved correction values survive recoverable failures; Back to billing confirms discard.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Select a patient, convert prescriptions, add service orders, review insurance and totals, issue an invoice, then record partial or full demo payments. Open receipts and history to review changes.

Use the public typed workspace and adapters shown in TypeScript. The authenticated demo API reads patient CSV and writes a separate billing CSV ledger. Replace adapters to connect another application.
Uses effective tenant-locked preferences for layout, theme, fonts, density, tables, dates and number display. Ledger currency comes from the API and is not converted by a display preference.

Input remains on screen during recoverable errors. Retry reuses operation identity. Load the latest ledger after a conflict and review your retained input. Browser-close draft restoration is not provided.

Fictional single-process demo: no real card processing, insurance submission, tax certification, pharmacy dispensing or accounting posting. Refunds reverse a full payment; invoices cannot be edited after issue.
Billing money keeps at least two decimal places so cents are not lost; general quantities retain your number preference.

paragraphs: Select a patient and encounter, choose the clinician and visit type, then enter history, examination, assessment and plan. Save a draft or review and complete. Open previous consultations to resume drafts or view completed notes.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: OP Registration keeps patient selection, registration, care and checkout in one page. Its five-step progress bar, patient strip, contextual side panels and bottom actions stay inside the existing application shell. All patient and encounter data comes from the authenticated demo API.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Search for a patient or create one using New patient. Confirm name and date of birth, review visit details, coverage and consent, then register and check in. Use the Nursing, Consultation, Orders, Billing and Checkout tabs without leaving this page. Sign the note before consultation charges post. Complete services before their charges post. Use the worklist to reopen a saved encounter.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: The server rejects missing identity and consent, duplicate active visits, stale record versions, invalid vital signs and payments above the balance. Signed notes use addenda. Pending results require an owner, due date and plan before checkout. Network retries reuse the operation ID. Saved drafts require identity and consent review again; tenant storage, retention and field exclusions apply. Reloading a conflicting record replaces the local form, so compare your values first.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Navigation access and write permission are checked by the demo API. The demo administrator can write; other authorized users can read. Effective theme, font scales, density, table settings, number/date/time formatting and language are inherited, including tenant locks. Currency comes from the ledger; formatting does not convert amounts. The five-step workflow and care tabs are fixed by this template, rather than the generic record navigation preference.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Compose RegistrationWorkspace with a RegistrationAdapter, ClinicalTemplateAdapter, authenticated scopeKey and PreferenceHost. The POST /op-registration endpoint loads configuration and executes versioned commands. Providers and services are read from CSV; encounters, appointments, payments and retry receipts share an atomic CSV snapshot scoped by tenant and application. Patient demographics reuse the existing patient API. These encounter records are separate from the older consultation and billing template stores. No real payer, payment, messaging or electronic-signature integration is connected.

paragraphs: This library previews backend-generated barcode and QR labels. Use dedicated pages for items, specimens, patient bands, documents, payment demos, batch printing and printer profiles.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Choose a template, paper profile, records and copies. Generate a preview, verify the identifying information, then open Print preview. Use actual size and disable browser headers. Save as PDF through the browser print dialog. Printing records a request, not confirmed physical delivery.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: The API rejects invalid records, excessive copies and labels that do not fit the paper. Reprints require permission and a reason. Retry preserves the operation identity. Payment links are synthetic; only an administrator can simulate payment status, and expired requests cannot be printed.

Your default stock does not fit this label. A compatible profile is selected for this preview; your saved default is unchanged. The tenant-locked printer stock does not fit this label. Ask your administrator to unlock it or select compatible stock.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The server isolates jobs by tenant, application and user. Tenant administrators control copy limits, reprints and locked printer profiles. Users can save an unlocked default profile. Screen preferences and language apply to the interface; printed codes retain approved dimensions and black-on-white contrast.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Inject LabelAdapter and effective preferences into LabelPrintingWorkspace. The authenticated POST /label-printing API owns record lookup, code generation and job history. Templates use JSON; synthetic records and scoped jobs use CSV. Replace the adapter for real applications. Payment providers, direct thermal printing and physical scanner certification remain external integrations.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Build a reusable frontend template with approved shared controls. This designer saves demo drafts, not published backend DCP forms.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Choose a section and add components from the palette. Drag handles or move buttons reorder items. Select a field to edit its label, required state, section, minimum or dropdown options. Preview uses temporary answers. Save design draft persists the design; Open saved design restores it.

After designing, select Live preview to try the current form without saving it. The preview shows the form title and hides editing controls. Validate preview checks your test answers. Reset preview clears only test answers; Design returns to editing and preserves the form. Preview answers never create business records.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Designs require titles, unique stable IDs and valid dropdown options. Limits are 20 sections, 100 fields and 50 options per field. Failed saves retain edits and retries reuse the operation ID. Conflicts require reopening the latest saved design after reviewing unsaved changes.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Only demo administrators can save designs. Drafts are isolated by tenant, application and user. Shared controls follow effective theme, density, typography and tenant locks. Preview does not save business answers or grant record access.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Inject DesignerAdapter and PreferenceHost into DcpDesignerWorkspace. The demo endpoint stores frontend template drafts in CSV snapshots. Backend DCP conversion, publication, datasets, rules and entity binding require the separate host adapter; no PostgreSQL or Java service is provisioned here.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Enter at least one search criterion, then select Search. Search anywhere matches whole words, quoted phrases and exclusions; the labelled fields support partial values. More filters includes ID type, nationality, residing country, gender, date of birth and status.

Choose table or cards and open patient details inline, in a dialog, or in a drawer. Previous and next navigate the current result page. Save a named preset to the API, or reuse recent searches kept only in this workspace session. Record, booking, encounter and 360 actions retain patient identity.

sections.title: Billing corrections and shared clinical rail
paragraphs: Open Invoices & payments, then View bill for the full invoice, insurance, line totals, receipts and revision history. Edit bill changes quantities, discount, insurance authorization and notes on unpaid issued invoices. Enter a correction reason and confirm. The API recalculates using its current tariffs and retains the previous invoice snapshot. Payment history, including refunds, prevents edits. Conflicts require loading and reviewing the latest ledger before saving again. Unsaved correction values survive recoverable failures; Back to billing confirms discard.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Select a patient, convert prescriptions, add service orders, review insurance and totals, issue an invoice, then record partial or full demo payments. Open receipts and history to review changes.

Use the public typed workspace and adapters shown in TypeScript. The authenticated demo API reads patient CSV and writes a separate billing CSV ledger. Replace adapters to connect another application.
Uses effective tenant-locked preferences for layout, theme, fonts, density, tables, dates and number display. Ledger currency comes from the API and is not converted by a display preference.

Input remains on screen during recoverable errors. Retry reuses operation identity. Load the latest ledger after a conflict and review your retained input. Browser-close draft restoration is not provided.

Fictional single-process demo: no real card processing, insurance submission, tax certification, pharmacy dispensing or accounting posting. Refunds reverse a full payment; invoices cannot be edited after issue.
Billing money keeps at least two decimal places so cents are not lost; general quantities retain your number preference.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Search for a patient or create one using New patient. Confirm name and date of birth, review visit details, coverage and consent, then register and check in. Use the Nursing, Consultation, Orders, Billing and Checkout tabs without leaving this page. Sign the note before consultation charges post. Complete services before their charges post. Use the worklist to reopen a saved encounter.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: The server rejects missing identity and consent, duplicate active visits, stale record versions, invalid vital signs and payments above the balance. Signed notes use addenda. Pending results require an owner, due date and plan before checkout. Network retries reuse the operation ID. Saved drafts require identity and consent review again; tenant storage, retention and field exclusions apply. Reloading a conflicting record replaces the local form, so compare your values first.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Navigation access and write permission are checked by the demo API. The demo administrator can write; other authorized users can read. Effective theme, font scales, density, table settings, number/date/time formatting and language are inherited, including tenant locks. Currency comes from the ledger; formatting does not convert amounts. The five-step workflow and care tabs are fixed by this template, rather than the generic record navigation preference.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Compose RegistrationWorkspace with a RegistrationAdapter, ClinicalTemplateAdapter, authenticated scopeKey and PreferenceHost. The POST /op-registration endpoint loads configuration and executes versioned commands. Providers and services are read from CSV; encounters, appointments, payments and retry receipts share an atomic CSV snapshot scoped by tenant and application. Patient demographics reuse the existing patient API. These encounter records are separate from the older consultation and billing template stores. No real payer, payment, messaging or electronic-signature integration is connected.

paragraphs: This library previews backend-generated barcode and QR labels. Use dedicated pages for items, specimens, patient bands, documents, payment demos, batch printing and printer profiles.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Choose a template, paper profile, records and copies. Generate a preview, verify the identifying information, then open Print preview. Use actual size and disable browser headers. Save as PDF through the browser print dialog. Printing records a request, not confirmed physical delivery.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: The API rejects invalid records, excessive copies and labels that do not fit the paper. Reprints require permission and a reason. Retry preserves the operation identity. Payment links are synthetic; only an administrator can simulate payment status, and expired requests cannot be printed.

Your default stock does not fit this label. A compatible profile is selected for this preview; your saved default is unchanged. The tenant-locked printer stock does not fit this label. Ask your administrator to unlock it or select compatible stock.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The server isolates jobs by tenant, application and user. Tenant administrators control copy limits, reprints and locked printer profiles. Users can save an unlocked default profile. Screen preferences and language apply to the interface; printed codes retain approved dimensions and black-on-white contrast.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Inject LabelAdapter and effective preferences into LabelPrintingWorkspace. The authenticated POST /label-printing API owns record lookup, code generation and job history. Templates use JSON; synthetic records and scoped jobs use CSV. Replace the adapter for real applications. Payment providers, direct thermal printing and physical scanner certification remain external integrations.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Build a reusable frontend template with approved shared controls. This designer saves demo drafts, not published backend DCP forms.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Choose a section and add components from the palette. Drag handles or move buttons reorder items. Select a field to edit its label, required state, section, minimum or dropdown options. Preview uses temporary answers. Save design draft persists the design; Open saved design restores it.

After designing, select Live preview to try the current form without saving it. The preview shows the form title and hides editing controls. Validate preview checks your test answers. Reset preview clears only test answers; Design returns to editing and preserves the form. Preview answers never create business records.

For dependent dropdowns, create Country with IN|India and AE|UAE. Create State with KL|Kerala, KA|Karnataka, AZ|Abu Dhabi and DU|Dubai. In State properties choose Depends on: Country, then map KL/KA to IN and AZ/DU to AE. Or insert the API-provided Country → State example. Preview loads options from the API, disables children until a valid parent is selected, and clears all descendants on parent changes. Retry failed lookups without losing parent selections. Validate preview checks matching parent/child IDs on the demo API without saving answers. Cycles, missing parents, unmapped options and more than five dependency links are rejected. Company → Branch uses the same generic configuration. Dataset imports and multi-parent conditions are not included.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Designs require titles, unique stable IDs and valid dropdown options. Limits are 20 sections, 100 fields and 50 options per field. Failed saves retain edits and retries reuse the operation ID. Conflicts require reopening the latest saved design after reviewing unsaved changes.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Only demo administrators can save designs. Drafts are isolated by tenant, application and user. Shared controls follow effective theme, density, typography and tenant locks. Preview does not save business answers or grant record access.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Inject DesignerAdapter and PreferenceHost into DcpDesignerWorkspace. The demo endpoint stores frontend template drafts in CSV snapshots. Backend DCP conversion, publication, datasets, rules and entity binding require the separate host adapter; no PostgreSQL or Java service is provisioned here.

sections.title: Page Library catalog
paragraphs: TypeScript examples, demo descriptions and user/integration guides are now in Page Library → List of pages. Individual pages open directly to their working screen. Patient search and selection stay available in those screens; existing API saves, preferences and tenant locks still apply.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Enter at least one search criterion, then select Search. Search anywhere matches whole words, quoted phrases and exclusions; the labelled fields support partial values. More filters includes ID type, nationality, residing country, gender, date of birth and status.

Choose table or cards and open patient details inline, in a dialog, or in a drawer. Previous and next navigate the current result page. Save a named preset to the API, or reuse recent searches kept only in this workspace session. Record, booking, encounter and 360 actions retain patient identity.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: The server rejects missing identity and consent, duplicate active visits, stale record versions, invalid vital signs and payments above the balance. Signed notes use addenda. Pending results require an owner, due date and plan before checkout. Network retries reuse the operation ID. Saved drafts require identity and consent review again; tenant storage, retention and field exclusions apply. Reloading a conflicting record replaces the local form, so compare your values first.

No real payer, payment, messaging or electronic-signature integration is connected.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Build a reusable frontend template with approved shared controls. This designer saves demo drafts, not published backend DCP forms.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Choose a section and add components from the palette. Drag handles or move buttons reorder items. Select a field to edit its label, required state, section, minimum or dropdown options. Preview uses temporary answers. Save design draft persists the design; Open saved design restores it.

After designing, select Live preview to try the current form without saving it. The preview shows the form title and hides editing controls. Validate preview checks your test answers. Reset preview clears only test answers; Design returns to editing and preserves the form. Preview answers never create business records.

For dependent dropdowns, create Country with IN|India and AE|UAE. Create State with KL|Kerala, KA|Karnataka, AZ|Abu Dhabi and DU|Dubai. In State properties choose Depends on: Country, then map KL/KA to IN and AZ/DU to AE. Or insert the API-provided Country → State example. Preview loads options from the API, disables children until a valid parent is selected, and clears all descendants on parent changes. Retry failed lookups without losing parent selections. Validate preview checks matching parent/child IDs on the demo API without saving answers. Cycles, missing parents, unmapped options and more than five dependency links are rejected. Company → Branch uses the same generic configuration. Dataset imports and multi-parent conditions are not included.

Open Manage value sets to create option lists shared within the current tenant and application. Only administrators can save new revisions. Use Relationships to select exact parent and child set revisions and map every child option. In field settings, choose an Option source revision; dependent fields also select their parent field and a compatible Shared relationship. Existing forms remain pinned when a new revision is saved. Adopting new revisions is explicit. Refresh catalog preserves edits; after a conflict, reopen the latest revision before saving. Catalog changes do not save or replace your current form. Inline options remain supported. Limits are 50 options per set and 100 retained revisions each for sets and relationships. Production DCP integration, inactive-value policies and publication approvals remain pending.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Designs require titles, unique stable IDs and valid dropdown options. Limits are 20 sections, 100 fields and 50 options per field. Failed saves retain edits and retries reuse the operation ID. Conflicts require reopening the latest saved design after reviewing unsaved changes.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Only demo administrators can save designs. Drafts are isolated by tenant, application and user. Shared controls follow effective theme, density, typography and tenant locks. Preview does not save business answers or grant record access.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Inject DesignerAdapter and PreferenceHost into DcpDesignerWorkspace. The demo endpoint stores frontend template drafts in CSV snapshots. Backend DCP conversion, publication, datasets, rules and entity binding require the separate host adapter; no PostgreSQL or Java service is provisioned here.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Enter at least one search criterion, then select Search. Search anywhere matches whole words, quoted phrases and exclusions; the labelled fields support partial values. More filters includes ID type, nationality, residing country, gender, date of birth and status.

Choose table or cards and open patient details inline, in a dialog, or in a drawer. Previous and next navigate the current result page. Save a named preset to the API, or reuse recent searches kept only in this workspace session. Record, booking, encounter and 360 actions retain patient identity.
Pass a ClinicalTemplateAdapter to ClinicalPatientWorkspace. The demo adapter uses the authenticated clinical-templates endpoint; business data and form metadata come from the API.
Saves validate fields and identity duplicates, enforce record versions and reuse operation IDs for retries. Review the latest record explicitly after a conflict.

sections.title: Billing corrections and shared clinical rail
paragraphs: Open Invoices & payments, then View bill for the full invoice, insurance, line totals, receipts and revision history. Edit bill changes quantities, discount, insurance authorization and notes on unpaid issued invoices. Enter a correction reason and confirm. The API recalculates using its current tariffs and retains the previous invoice snapshot. Payment history, including refunds, prevents edits. Conflicts require loading and reviewing the latest ledger before saving again. Unsaved correction values survive recoverable failures; Back to billing confirms discard.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Select a patient, convert prescriptions, add service orders, review insurance and totals, issue an invoice, then record partial or full demo payments. Open receipts and history to review changes.

Use the public typed workspace and adapters shown in TypeScript. The authenticated demo API reads patient CSV and writes a separate billing CSV ledger. Replace adapters to connect another application.
Uses effective tenant-locked preferences for layout, theme, fonts, density, tables, dates and number display. Ledger currency comes from the API and is not converted by a display preference.

Input remains on screen during recoverable errors. Retry reuses operation identity. Load the latest ledger after a conflict and review your retained input. Browser-close draft restoration is not provided.

Fictional single-process demo: no real card processing, insurance submission, tax certification, pharmacy dispensing or accounting posting. Refunds reverse a full payment; invoices cannot be edited after issue.
Billing money keeps at least two decimal places so cents are not lost; general quantities retain your number preference.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Select a patient and encounter, choose the clinician and visit type, then enter history, examination, assessment and plan. Save a draft or review and complete. Open previous consultations to resume drafts or view completed notes.

Twelve sections are available through one-click tabs inside three columns: visit, background, vitals, allergies, assessment, systems, results, procedures, plan, medicines, referrals and education. Tab counts show entered fields. Values stay when switching sections. New optional fields save through the demo API; older notes remain readable. Vitals are manually entered, and prescriptions, procedures, referrals and consent remain documentation notes rather than dispatched or signed actions.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Search for a patient or create one using New patient. Confirm name and date of birth, review visit details, coverage and consent, then register and check in. sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: The server rejects missing identity and consent, duplicate active visits, stale record versions, invalid vital signs and payments above the balance. Signed notes use addenda. Pending results require an owner, due date and plan before checkout. Network retries reuse the operation ID. Saved drafts require identity and consent review again; tenant storage, retention and field exclusions apply. Reloading a conflicting record replaces the local form, so compare your values first.

sections.title: Access and preferences

Currency comes from the ledger; formatting does not convert amounts. The five-step workflow and care tabs are fixed by this template, rather than the generic record navigation preference.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Compose RegistrationWorkspace with a RegistrationAdapter, ClinicalTemplateAdapter, authenticated scopeKey and PreferenceHost. The POST /op-registration endpoint loads configuration and executes versioned commands. Providers and services are read from CSV; encounters, appointments, payments and retry receipts share an atomic CSV snapshot scoped by tenant and application. Patient demographics reuse the existing patient API. These encounter records are separate from the older consultation and billing template stores. No real payer, payment, messaging or electronic-signature integration is connected.

paragraphs: This library previews backend-generated barcode and QR labels. Use dedicated pages for items, specimens, patient bands, documents, payment demos, batch printing and printer profiles.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Choose a template, paper profile, records and copies. Generate a preview, verify the identifying information, then open Print preview. Use actual size and disable browser headers. Save as PDF through the browser print dialog. Printing records a request, not confirmed physical delivery.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: The API rejects invalid records, excessive copies and labels that do not fit the paper. Reprints require permission and a reason. Retry preserves the operation identity. Payment links are synthetic; only an administrator can simulate payment status, and expired requests cannot be printed.

Your default stock does not fit this label. A compatible profile is selected for this preview; your saved default is unchanged. The tenant-locked printer stock does not fit this label. Ask your administrator to unlock it or select compatible stock.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The server isolates jobs by tenant, application and user. Tenant administrators control copy limits, reprints and locked printer profiles. Users can save an unlocked default profile. Screen preferences and language apply to the interface; printed codes retain approved dimensions and black-on-white contrast.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Inject LabelAdapter and effective preferences into LabelPrintingWorkspace. The authenticated POST /label-printing API owns record lookup, code generation and job history. Templates use JSON; synthetic records and scoped jobs use CSV. Replace the adapter for real applications. Payment providers, direct thermal printing and physical scanner certification remain external integrations.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Build a reusable frontend template with approved shared controls. This designer saves demo drafts, not published backend DCP forms.

Upload UTF-8 CSV, map ID and label columns, then review every row. Apply replaces the option editor only; Save new revision commits the complete dataset through the API. Existing published references are unchanged. Import 1–50 option rows. Larger datasets are not supported here. Use a unique nonblank ID (up to 80 characters) and a label (up to 160). Pipes and line breaks are not supported in this editor.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Choose a section and add components from the palette. Drag handles or move buttons reorder items. Select a field to edit its label, required state, section, minimum or dropdown options. Preview uses temporary answers. Save design draft persists the design; Open saved design restores it.

After designing, select Live preview to try the current form without saving it. The preview shows the form title and hides editing controls. Validate preview checks your test answers. Reset preview clears only test answers; Design returns to editing and preserves the form. Preview answers never create business records.

For dependent dropdowns, create Country with IN|India and AE|UAE. Create State with KL|Kerala, KA|Karnataka, AZ|Abu Dhabi and DU|Dubai. In State properties choose Depends on: Country, then map KL/KA to IN and AZ/DU to AE. Or insert the API-provided Country → State example. Preview loads options from the API, disables children until a valid parent is selected, and clears all descendants on parent changes. Retry failed lookups without losing parent selections. Validate preview checks matching parent/child IDs on the demo API without saving answers. Cycles, missing parents, unmapped options and more than five dependency links are rejected. Company → Branch uses the same generic configuration. Dataset imports and multi-parent conditions are not included.

Open Manage value sets to create option lists shared within the current tenant and application. Only administrators can save new revisions. Use Relationships to select exact parent and child set revisions and map every child option. In field settings, choose an Option source revision; dependent fields also select their parent field and a compatible Shared relationship. Existing forms remain pinned when a new revision is saved. Adopting new revisions is explicit. Refresh catalog preserves edits; after a conflict, reopen the latest revision before saving. Catalog changes do not save or replace your current form. Inline options remain supported. Limits are 50 options per set and 100 retained revisions each for sets and relationships. Production DCP integration, inactive-value policies and publication approvals remain pending.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Designs require titles, unique stable IDs and valid dropdown options. Limits are 20 sections, 100 fields and 50 options per field. Failed saves retain edits and retries reuse the operation ID. Conflicts require reopening the latest saved design after reviewing unsaved changes.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Only demo administrators can save designs. Drafts are isolated by tenant, application and user. Shared controls follow effective theme, density, typography and tenant locks. Preview does not save business answers or grant record access.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Inject DesignerAdapter and PreferenceHost into DcpDesignerWorkspace. The demo endpoint stores frontend template drafts in CSV snapshots. Backend DCP conversion, publication, datasets, rules and entity binding require the separate host adapter; no PostgreSQL or Java service is provisioned here.

sections.title: Identity device workflows
paragraphs: Synthetic identity workflow only. No real card, passport, fingerprint or face is captured.
Use a separate manual workflow when biometrics are unavailable or declined. This demo never stores biometric images or templates.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Enter at least one search criterion, then select Search. Search anywhere matches whole words, quoted phrases and exclusions; the labelled fields support partial values. More filters includes ID type, nationality, residing country, gender, date of birth and status.

Choose table or cards and open patient details inline, in a dialog, or in a drawer. Previous and next navigate the current result page. Save a named preset to the API, or reuse recent searches kept only in this workspace session. Record, booking, encounter and 360 actions retain patient identity.
Pass a ClinicalTemplateAdapter to ClinicalPatientWorkspace. The demo adapter uses the authenticated clinical-templates endpoint; business data and form metadata come from the API.
Saves validate fields and identity duplicates, enforce record versions and reuse operation IDs for retries. Review the latest record explicitly after a conflict.

sections.title: Billing corrections and shared clinical rail
paragraphs: Open Invoices & payments, then View bill for the full invoice, insurance, line totals, receipts and revision history. Edit bill changes quantities, discount, insurance authorization and notes on unpaid issued invoices. Enter a correction reason and confirm. The API recalculates using its current tariffs and retains the previous invoice snapshot. Payment history, including refunds, prevents edits. Conflicts require loading and reviewing the latest ledger before saving again. Unsaved correction values survive recoverable failures; Back to billing confirms discard.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Search for a patient or create one using New patient. Confirm name and date of birth, review visit details, coverage and consent, then register and check in. sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: The server rejects missing identity and consent, duplicate active visits, stale record versions, invalid vital signs and payments above the balance. Signed notes use addenda. Pending results require an owner, due date and plan before checkout. Network retries reuse the operation ID. Saved drafts require identity and consent review again; tenant storage, retention and field exclusions apply. Reloading a conflicting record replaces the local form, so compare your values first.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Navigation access and write permission are checked by the demo API. The demo administrator can write; other authorized users can read. Effective theme, font scales, density, table settings, number/date/time formatting and language are inherited, including tenant locks. Currency comes from the ledger; formatting does not convert amounts. The five-step workflow and care tabs are fixed by this template, rather than the generic record navigation preference.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Compose RegistrationWorkspace with a RegistrationAdapter, ClinicalTemplateAdapter, authenticated scopeKey and PreferenceHost. The POST /op-registration endpoint loads configuration and executes versioned commands. Providers and services are read from CSV; encounters, appointments, payments and retry receipts share an atomic CSV snapshot scoped by tenant and application. Patient demographics reuse the existing patient API. These encounter records are separate from the older consultation and billing template stores. No real payer, payment, messaging or electronic-signature integration is connected.

paragraphs: This library previews backend-generated barcode and QR labels. Use dedicated pages for items, specimens, patient bands, documents, payment demos, batch printing and printer profiles.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Choose a template, paper profile, records and copies. Generate a preview, verify the identifying information, then open Print preview. Use actual size and disable browser headers. Save as PDF through the browser print dialog. Printing records a request, not confirmed physical delivery.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: The API rejects invalid records, excessive copies and labels that do not fit the paper. Reprints require permission and a reason. Retry preserves the operation identity. Payment links are synthetic; only an administrator can simulate payment status, and expired requests cannot be printed.

Your default stock does not fit this label. A compatible profile is selected for this preview; your saved default is unchanged. The tenant-locked printer stock does not fit this label. Ask your administrator to unlock it or select compatible stock.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The server isolates jobs by tenant, application and user. Tenant administrators control copy limits, reprints and locked printer profiles. Users can save an unlocked default profile. Screen preferences and language apply to the interface; printed codes retain approved dimensions and black-on-white contrast.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Inject LabelAdapter and effective preferences into LabelPrintingWorkspace. The authenticated POST /label-printing API owns record lookup, code generation and job history. Templates use JSON; synthetic records and scoped jobs use CSV. Replace the adapter for real applications. Payment providers, direct thermal printing and physical scanner certification remain external integrations.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Choose a template, paper profile, records and copies. Generate a preview, verify the identifying information, then open Print preview. Use actual size and disable browser headers. Save as PDF through the browser print dialog. Printing records a request, not confirmed physical delivery.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: The API rejects invalid records, excessive copies and labels that do not fit the paper. Reprints require permission and a reason. Retry preserves the operation identity. Payment links are synthetic; only an administrator can simulate payment status, and expired requests cannot be printed.

Your default stock does not fit this label. A compatible profile is selected for this preview; your saved default is unchanged. The tenant-locked printer stock does not fit this label. Ask your administrator to unlock it or select compatible stock.

sections.title: Integration

Payment providers, direct thermal printing and physical scanner certification remain external integrations.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Answer owner type → Application trigger → Save design draft → Submit for review → Approve design → Publish version → Published forms → Form release → Owner record → Load owner form → Save answer draft → Submit answers
Form layout → All sections → Section tabs → Step by step → Form columns

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Rules are typed and cycle-checked. Hidden values are retained; visibility does not grant access. Calculations are recomputed by the API.
Minimum → Maximum → Whole numbers only → Minimum length → Maximum length → Text format → Normalize before validation → Visible when → Required when → Read-only when → Calculation

Upload CSV or XLSX, choose a worksheet and map text ID/label columns. Review all rows before replacing the editor. Saving creates one complete revision; old form references stay pinned. → Import 1–1,000 option rows per revision. → The demo catalog has reached its 10,000 retained-option budget. Use the production dataset adapter for larger workloads. → Workbook rejected. Use a plain XLSX with at most 10 sheets, 80 columns and 1,000 data rows per sheet, without macros or external links. → Formula cells are not allowed. Export values-only before importing.

sections.title: Access and preferences

sections.title: Billing corrections and shared clinical rail
paragraphs: Open Invoices & payments, then View bill for the full invoice, insurance, line totals, receipts and revision history. Edit bill changes quantities, discount, insurance authorization and notes on unpaid issued invoices. Enter a correction reason and confirm. The API recalculates using its current tariffs and retains the previous invoice snapshot. Payment history, including refunds, prevents edits. Conflicts require loading and reviewing the latest ledger before saving again. Unsaved correction values survive recoverable failures; Back to billing confirms discard.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: The API rejects invalid records, excessive copies and labels that do not fit the paper. Reprints require permission and a reason. Retry preserves the operation identity. sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The server isolates jobs by tenant, application and user. Tenant administrators control copy limits, reprints and locked printer profiles. Users can save an unlocked default profile. sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Inject LabelAdapter and effective preferences into LabelPrintingWorkspace. The authenticated POST /label-printing API owns record lookup, code generation and job history. Templates use JSON; synthetic records and scoped jobs use CSV. Replace the adapter for real applications. Payment providers, direct thermal printing and physical scanner certification remain external integrations.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Compose reusable forms with shared controls, layouts, translations and rules. Designs and published answer examples use the demo API. Backend contract runtime demonstrates the supplied DCP v1 contract separately; the visual design is not a backend Dcp.Form payload.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Add fields and sections, choose presentation and label language, and preview. Dropdowns can require up to four parents; map each child option to every parent. Import CSV/XLSX into a value set, review and save its revision. Save the design, select an owner type, review, approve and publish. Compare a saved release with the current design. Published forms load owner answers and show revision history.

Select a section and enable Repeat this section to add a bounded group of rows. Set minimum and maximum rows. Each row retains its own identity, values and validation messages. Calculations run per row; changing a shared parent clears dependent selections in every row. Copying a sample remaps its internal field references. Designer repetition currently supports one row level; nested collections are available in the separate v1 runtime.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Preview checks required values, types, ranges, normalization, calculations and dropdown membership. Any parent change clears dependent selections. The v1 runtime previews edits with server rules, supports repeating rows, and keeps false as a valid present Boolean value. A 422 response displays validation errors and does not confirm a save. A conflict or uncertain save requires reviewing the server record; writes are not automatically retried.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Effective preferences and tenant locks still apply. Tenant-authored labels fall back from the selected language to English, then the original label. Shared recovery follows tenant retention and field exclusions and stores no browser-local copy. Recovery requires the same record revision and checksum. Draft Center lists DCP recovery drafts; open the designer and Backend contract runtime to review them. Masked and nonwritable v1 fields cannot be edited. Demo navigation and roles are not production field authorization.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Use DcpDesignerWorkspace for frontend authoring and DcpHostRuntime with createDcpRuntimeAdapter for host-bound v1 forms. The application supplies authenticated load, preview and save routes, scope identity and optional shared recovery scope. Revisions remain strings; collection rows use _id; omitted values retain data and null clears explicitly. Jira PLIBRYBEND-206 contains the verified backend handoff and remaining backend work. Advanced enterprise contracts and actual production/native acceptance are not yet complete.

sections.title: Identity device workflows
paragraphs: Synthetic identity workflow only. No real card, passport, fingerprint or face is captured.
Use a separate manual workflow when biometrics are unavailable or declined. This demo never stores biometric images or templates.

releases.summary: Reports, ERP1, ERP2 and School reference frontend modules imported as separately reusable packages, composed inside the existing shell with host-authenticated adapters.
knownIssues: Native-speaker translation review for the 152 reference guides is pending for Arabic, Hindi and Malayalam; translated text has not yet been authored, so the current status is incomplete rather than reviewed.
Interactive/browser acceptance, both host builds and cross-cutting impact-receipt review for the reference module import remain separate, in-progress work tracked by the root/implementation agents.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Search for an existing customer before creating another record. Open a row to inspect its details. Use New or Edit only when those actions are available for your role. Complete the required identity and contact fields, review validation messages, then save.
After saving, return to the worklist and verify the customer appears with the expected details. If another session changed the record, reload and compare before resubmitting.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Search existing patient records before creating a record. Verify identity using your organization’s approved registration procedure. Open the selected record and review the field reference for required registration details.

Correct displayed validation errors before saving. If you suspect a duplicate, follow your organization’s duplicate-review procedure rather than creating additional records. This guide describes software operation and does not provide clinical advice.

sections.title: Own Settings
paragraphs: Choose the module to open on your next sign-in or application home visit. Direct page links stay unchanged. Application default uses your existing start-up settings.

sections.title: Purpose
paragraphs: Use Preferences to choose the appearance, language and behavior of your application.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Select a preference group and adjust an available setting. Changes save automatically. Managed settings are enforced by your tenant administrator. Imports and resets cannot override a lock.

Administrators with preference-management permission can open Preference policies, choose default values and lock settings. Save policy applies the policy to this tenant and application. Unlocking restores saved personal choices.

paragraphs: Read page guides, published releases, patches and change notices for this application.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Choose a guide or a release. Search by title, module or guide content. Select a release to read the guide snapshot for that version. Open What’s new to find changes affecting pages you can access.

paragraphs: Sanitized application diagnostics collected by Sentinel.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Filter incidents by page and status. Open an incident to inspect sanitized diagnostics. Move it to Investigating or Resolved. A recurring failure reopens a resolved incident.

sections.title: Purpose
paragraphs: Find and resume your unfinished work.

Effective preferences and tenant locks still apply. Tenant-authored labels fall back from the selected language to English, then the original label. Shared recovery follows tenant retention and field exclusions and stores no browser-local copy. Recovery requires the same record revision and checksum. Draft Center lists DCP recovery drafts; open the designer and Backend contract runtime to review them. Masked and nonwritable v1 fields cannot be edited. Demo navigation and roles are not production field authorization.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Opening never submits a record or approval. Reselect CSV files to restore mappings. Refresh if another window changed a draft. Each application has its own recovery center.
Draft storage is enabled by your tenant policy. Only service-acknowledged changes are recoverable.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Enter at least one search criterion, then select Search. Search anywhere matches whole words, quoted phrases and exclusions; the labelled fields support partial values. More filters includes ID type, nationality, residing country, gender, date of birth and status.

Choose table or cards and open patient details inline, in a dialog, or in a drawer. Previous and next navigate the current result page. Save a named preset to the API, or reuse recent searches kept only in this workspace session. Record, booking, encounter and 360 actions retain patient identity.
Pass a ClinicalTemplateAdapter to ClinicalPatientWorkspace. The demo adapter uses the authenticated clinical-templates endpoint; business data and form metadata come from the API.
Saves validate fields and identity duplicates, enforce record versions and reuse operation IDs for retries. Review the latest record explicitly after a conflict.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Search for a patient or create one using New patient. Confirm name and date of birth, review visit details, coverage and consent, then register and check in. Use the Nursing, Consultation, Orders, Billing and Checkout tabs without leaving this page. Sign the note before consultation charges post. Complete services before their charges post. Use the worklist to reopen a saved encounter.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: The server rejects missing identity and consent, duplicate active visits, stale record versions, invalid vital signs and payments above the balance. Signed notes use addenda. Pending results require an owner, due date and plan before checkout. Network retries reuse the operation ID. Saved drafts require identity and consent review again; tenant storage, retention and field exclusions apply. Reloading a conflicting record replaces the local form, so compare your values first.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Navigation access and write permission are checked by the demo API. The demo administrator can write; other authorized users can read. Effective theme, font scales, density, table settings, number/date/time formatting and language are inherited, including tenant locks. Currency comes from the ledger; formatting does not convert amounts. The five-step workflow and care tabs are fixed by this template, rather than the generic record navigation preference.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Compose RegistrationWorkspace with a RegistrationAdapter, ClinicalTemplateAdapter, authenticated scopeKey and PreferenceHost. The POST /op-registration endpoint loads configuration and executes versioned commands. Providers and services are read from CSV; encounters, appointments, payments and retry receipts share an atomic CSV snapshot scoped by tenant and application. Patient demographics reuse the existing patient API. These encounter records are separate from the older consultation and billing template stores. No real payer, payment, messaging or electronic-signature integration is connected.

paragraphs: This library previews backend-generated barcode and QR labels. Use dedicated pages for items, specimens, patient bands, documents, payment demos, batch printing and printer profiles.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Choose a template, paper profile, records and copies. Generate a preview, verify the identifying information, then open Print preview. Use actual size and disable browser headers. Save as PDF through the browser print dialog. Printing records a request, not confirmed physical delivery.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: The API rejects invalid records, excessive copies and labels that do not fit the paper. Reprints require permission and a reason. Retry preserves the operation identity. Payment links are synthetic; only an administrator can simulate payment status, and expired requests cannot be printed.

Your default stock does not fit this label. A compatible profile is selected for this preview; your saved default is unchanged. The tenant-locked printer stock does not fit this label. Ask your administrator to unlock it or select compatible stock.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The server isolates jobs by tenant, application and user. Tenant administrators control copy limits, reprints and locked printer profiles. Users can save an unlocked default profile. Screen preferences and language apply to the interface; printed codes retain approved dimensions and black-on-white contrast.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Inject LabelAdapter and effective preferences into LabelPrintingWorkspace. The authenticated POST /label-printing API owns record lookup, code generation and job history. Templates use JSON; synthetic records and scoped jobs use CSV. Replace the adapter for real applications. Payment providers, direct thermal printing and physical scanner certification remain external integrations.
