sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Sign in through the host and choose an available School view in the header. The server confirms that your account may use the selected role before loading its dashboard.

2. Review the role's headline metrics (for example admin: attendance and collections; teacher: today's schedule and pending grading; student: schedule, attendance and open assignments; librarian: issues, overdues and stock; accountant: billed/collected/outstanding).
3. Use the dashboard shortcuts to jump into the relevant page (attendance, assignments, fees, library and so on).
4. A parent uses the child switcher to move between their own children's cards; each card reloads that child's own statistics.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: If the initial lookups (school calendar, profile, classes, subjects or teachers) fail to load, the module shows an error state with retry instead of a broken dashboard.
A trend figure (for example an attendance or collections change) is shown only when the server actually returns one; the client never invents a trend.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The server resolves and confirms the authenticated user's role; an unconfirmed or unknown role is never treated as admin, and the client shows an access state instead of a portal in that case.
A parent's requests are scoped to their own children only; the server enforces that ownership.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: The header selects a School view; it does not grant permissions. The session endpoint confirms the effective role from authenticated server entitlements, and every School request carries the selected module for server validation. Other browser tabs keep their own selected view.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Admissions tracks prospective students through the enrolment funnel, from applied to enrolled, at /admissions.
Applications are shown as cards on a stage board; the applicant's parent contact stays visible at every stage.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Review the funnel counts (applications, conversion) and the board of applications grouped by stage.
2. Use "New application"/"Create application" to add one, entering the applicant's name and the grade they are applying for.
3. Advance an application by dragging its card to the next stage, or use the stage arrows; "Advance to" shows the next available stage.
4. Use "Decline" to close an application, or "Enrol & register" once an application reaches its final stage, which continues into student registration.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: An application dropped on an invalid stage, or an incomplete new application, is rejected before the stage change or creation is saved.
"Application {id} created" confirms a successful save; a failed request keeps the entered values so the form can be retried.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Creating and advancing applications is limited to the admin role.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Applications are read and written through the school adapter's admissions resource; the server assigns the application number and applied date.

fields.label: Applicant name
fields.help: Full name of the prospective student.

fields.label: Applying for
fields.help: Grade the applicant is applying to join.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Assignments lets teachers set and grade class work, and lets students turn it in, at /assignments.
The page adapts to role: teachers see class averages and grading progress; students see what is due and their own submission state.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Teachers: use "New assignment" to create one, then "Publish" to make it visible to the class (or "Save draft" to hold it back); "Close submissions"/"Reopen" controls whether students can still submit.
2. Teachers: open a submission to grade it, entering marks (0 to the assignment's maximum) and optional feedback; "No work received" marks ungraded, unsubmitted work.
3. Students: open an assignment due and use "Submit"/"Turn in" with the answer text and any attachment; a submission after the due date is recorded as late.
4. Both roles can track progress from the class-average and "Overdue"/"Due" indicators on the list.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Marks outside 0 to the assignment's maximum are rejected with "Marks must be between 0 and {max}" before the grade is saved.
Saving, turning in or sending is disabled while an attachment is uploading, failed or refused; a failed upload keeps the file selected so "Retry upload" can resend the identical payload.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Only the assigned class's teacher may publish, close or grade an assignment; a student may only submit to their own class's assignments.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Assignments are created and read/patched (with attachments) through the school adapter's assignments resource; submissions are managed through the matching submissions resource, which enforces the 0..max marks rule and the submitted/graded counters on the server.

fields.label: Title
fields.help: Shown to the class once published.

fields.label: Due
fields.help: Deadline after which a submission is marked late.

fields.label: Max marks
rules: Grades must fall between 0 and this value.

fields.label: Status
fields.help: Draft, published, or closed for submissions.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Attendance records daily class presence and lets students/parents request leave, at /attendance.
A teacher marks a whole class register for a date; students and parents instead see that student's own attendance history.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Teachers: pick a class and date, mark each student Present/Absent/Late/Excused (a missing mark defaults to Present), then "Save register".
2. Teachers: use "All present" to mark the whole class present in one step, and "Reset" to discard unsaved changes to the register.
3. Students/parents: review the attendance calendar and the last-60-day summary (present/absent/late/excused), and use "Submit request" to send a leave request with a date range and reason.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A register cannot be saved with an invalid payload; the server rejects an incomplete request before any row is stored.
"Register saved" confirms a successful save; weekends and future dates never accept a status and show as such on the calendar.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Only the class's own teacher may mark or edit that class's register; a parent can only submit leave requests and view attendance for their own children.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: The register is read/written through the school adapter's attendance resource (by class and date for marking, by student and month for history); leave requests are created as a real record through the leave-requests resource, not a toast.

fields.label: Status
fields.help: Per-student attendance mark for the selected date.
rules: Available options: Present, Absent, Late, Excused.

fields.label: From
fields.help: First day of the requested leave.

fields.label: To
fields.help: Last day of the requested leave.

fields.label: Reason
fields.help: Reason shown to the reviewing teacher/office.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Calendar shows the school's month view of scheduled events, at /calendar.
Events are shown alongside the same term structure already used by exams and reports.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Use "Previous month"/"Next month" (or "Today") to navigate; "Coming up" lists the next events regardless of the month shown.
2. Use "Add event"/"Add calendar event" to create one, entering title, type, location, start and (optionally, for multi-day events) end.
3. Use "Export" to download the calendar for use in an external calendar application.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: An event with a start after its end (for multi-day events) is rejected before saving.
A day with more events than fit shows a "+N more" indicator rather than silently hiding them.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Creating events is limited to the admin role; every role can view the calendar.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Events are read and written through the school adapter's events resource via the injected host adapter.

fields.label: Title
fields.help: Shown on the calendar and in Coming up.

fields.label: Type
fields.help: Categorises the event on the calendar.

fields.label: Location
fields.help: Optional venue, for example Main campus.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Classes lists the school's class/sections with their strength, class teacher and average score, at /classes.
Each class links to its own attendance register, mark list and timetable.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Review the class list, including occupancy (% seats filled), class teacher, GPA and gender split.
2. Use "Add class"/"Create class" to add a section, entering grade, section, name, room, capacity, stream and class teacher.
3. From a class, jump to its "Attendance", "Mark list" or "Timetable" using the shown shortcuts.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Creating a class requires grade, section and a capacity greater than zero; the server initializes its strength and average score at zero.
A class teacher can only be assigned from the teacher directory; an invalid selection is rejected before saving.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Creating or editing classes is limited to the admin role.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Classes are read and written through the school adapter's classes resource; strength changes automatically when a student is admitted or transferred, rather than being edited directly here.

fields.label: Grade
fields.help: Grade level the class belongs to.

fields.label: Capacity
fields.help: Maximum seats; used to compute % occupancy.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Exams schedules terms and papers and shows admit-card/day-of information, at /exams.
Students see their own schedule and checklist; staff see the scheduling and invigilation view.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Staff: use "Schedule paper"/"Schedule" to set a subject, date, time and room for a term's paper.
2. Students: review "Next paper" and the full schedule, then use "Print admit card" before the exam.

3. Review the "Exam-day checklist" (arrive 15 minutes early with admit card and ID; only transparent pencil cases and approved calculators; phones handed to the invigilator) and, for staff, "My duties" for invigilation assignments.
4. After marking, review the "Mark list" for a paper, and "Max"/"Marked" counts to track completion.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Scheduling a paper for a subject/date/room already in use for that class is rejected as a clash before saving.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Scheduling papers and viewing full invigilation duties is limited to the teacher and admin roles; students see only their own class's published schedule.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Exam schedules are read and written through the school adapter's exam resources; marks entry uses the same marks resource described for the Marks page.

fields.label: Room
fields.help: Room the paper is held in.
rules: Cannot clash with another paper in the same room/time.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Fees manages student invoices and payment collection for finance staff, and shows a family's own balance for students/parents, at /fees.
Payment actions record synthetic payment information through the API; they never create a live bank or payment-provider transaction.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Finance staff: filter by class/term/status, then open an invoice and use "Collect"/"Collect payment" to record an amount and method.
2. Finance staff: use "Remind all" to send payment reminders by email/SMS to every family with an outstanding invoice in the current filter.
3. Students/parents: review "Balance due"/"Paid" for each invoice and the sibling-discount and late-fee policy shown on the page.
4. Use "Print" to produce a receipt/statement for a settled or partial invoice.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: An amount greater than the invoice's outstanding balance is rejected by the server rather than silently capped; an amount of zero is a no-op. A successful payment returns the server-issued status (Paid/Partial) and, when actually generated, a receipt number; the client never invents a receipt number or claims an email was sent unless the server reports it.
The student's overall fee status (Overdue > Partial > Due > Paid) is recomputed by the server after every payment, not calculated locally.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Recording payments and sending reminders is limited to the accountant and admin roles; students and parents can only view their own (or their child's) invoices.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Invoices are read through the school adapter's invoices resource and updated with the payment amount and method; reminders use the invoice-reminders action; the fee tariff and sibling/late-fee policy come from the fee-structure resource.

fields.label: Amount
fields.help: Amount being collected against this invoice.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Library manages the book catalogue and issue/return/reservation workflow, at /library.
Members without an available copy can place a reservation instead of an issue.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Search and filter the catalogue by category or availability; use "Add book" to register a new title with author, ISBN, category, publisher, year, copies and shelf.
2. Use "Issue"/"Issue book" against a member for an available title, or "Renew" an existing loan (14-day loans, per the catalogue note).
3. Use "Return" to close a loan; the server computes any fine and the client shows exactly that figure.
4. When "All copies out", use the reservation action instead; the server decides whether it is filled immediately or waitlisted.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Issuing a book with no available copies is refused with "No copies available. Place a reservation instead."; issuing an unknown book id returns "Book not found".

After an issue, renewal or return, the client reloads the authoritative stock (available copies) from the server rather than adjusting it locally, so a client-side estimate cannot silently drift from the server's record.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Adding books and processing issues/returns is limited to librarian/admin roles; any registered user may request a reservation.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Books, issues and reservations are managed through the school adapter's books, issues and reservations resources; a return's fine and the post-return stock count are both authoritative server values.

fields.label: Copies
fields.help: Total copies owned; sets initial availability.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Live lists scheduled, in-progress and ended live classes, at /live.
Selecting a live or upcoming session opens the live-room; recording, chat and polls exchange state through the API only, and no audio or video leaves the browser in this reference module.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Review sessions by status (Scheduled/Live/Ended), computed from each session's start time and duration against the server clock.
2. Use "Start instant class"/"Start now" to begin an unscheduled session immediately, or "Schedule" to plan one for later.
3. Use "Join lobby"/"Join now" to enter a session; a host can toggle "Recording" and see "Average attendance" after it ends.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: If a leave/end call fails, the user stays in the room rather than being silently dropped.
"Recordings stream from your media storage in production." - this reference module never stores or relays actual audio/video.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Only the assigned teacher (host) can end a session, launch/close polls, or mute/lower hands for other participants; students may raise a hand, vote and send chat messages.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Session listing and status use the school adapter's live resource; in-room state is exchanged through a polled room-state endpoint and an actions endpoint for join/leave/end/message/poll/hand/recording/mute/camera/reaction.

fields.label: Title
fields.help: Session name shown on the list.

fields.label: Class
fields.help: Class the session is held for.

fields.label: Duration (minutes)
fields.help: Session length used to compute its end and status.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Marks is the term-wise mark-entry grid and report-card source for a class, at /marks.
Entry stays open only while the term is scheduled and the paper is marked as open for entry.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Choose a class and term to load its subject columns and student rows; use the arrow keys to move between cells while entering marks.
2. Enter each student's mark per subject (within 0 and the paper's maximum), then "Save marks"; "Reset" discards unsaved edits.
3. Review "Class average", "Rank" and the grade scale (A+ >=90, A >=80, B+ >=70, B >=60, C >=50, D >=40, F) shown on the grid.
4. Use "CSV"/"Print" to export the grid, or open a student's own report card, which pulls the same marks across terms.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A mark outside 0 and the paper's maximum is rejected with "Marks must be between 0 and {max}" and highlighted as "Some marks are out of range" before saving.
A scheduled (not-yet-sat) term always returns null marks rather than a fabricated zero.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Only the class/subject teacher (or admin) may enter or edit marks for a class; students and parents only view the resulting report card.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: The grid is loaded and saved through the school adapter's marks resource with per-student, per-subject entries; the report card is computed by the server (rank, class average, grade) rather than the client.

fields.label: Mark
fields.help: Score for one student in one subject for the selected term.
rules: Must be between 0 and the paper's maximum.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Messages is the school's internal messaging inbox between staff, students, parents and school offices, at /messages.
Conversations are threads; opening one marks it read.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Search conversations, or use "New message" to start one, choosing a recipient from office contacts (for example the principal, school office or finance - contact labels, not separate login roles) or the teacher directory.
2. Write the message (Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line) and optionally "Attach" a file, then "Send".
3. Review the thread; a failed send keeps the draft text and any attachment so it can be retried.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: "Message not sent - {reason}" shows the exact server error and keeps the composed message on screen; "Message sent to {name}" confirms delivery.
Sending is disabled while an attachment is uploading, failed or refused.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: A user can only see and open threads they are a participant of; the server appends any reply rather than the client fabricating one.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Threads are read and updated through the school adapter's threads resource (marking read, or appending a message with its attachments); contacts for new messages come from the contacts and teachers resources.

fields.label: To
rules: Required to start a new message.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Notices posts school-wide or audience-targeted announcements, at /notices.
A pinned notice stays at the top of the list for its audience.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Review notices, newest first, with pinned ones at the top; use "Pin"/"Pin to top" or unpin as needed.
2. Use "Post notice"/"Post a notice" to add one, choosing the audience and writing the message (at least 10 characters).
3. Use "Delete" to remove a notice; the confirmation states that recipients will no longer see it.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A message under 10 characters is rejected before posting.
"Notice posted to {audience}" confirms success; deleting asks "Delete “{title}”? Recipients will no longer see it." before removing it.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Posting, pinning and deleting notices is limited to the admin and teacher roles; the audience selector controls who receives it, enforced server-side.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Notices are read, written, pinned and deleted through the school adapter's notices resource.

fields.label: Audience
fields.help: Who the notice is shown to.

fields.label: Pinned
fields.help: Keeps the notice at the top of its audience's list.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Quizzes lists published and draft quizzes; students see their own attempts and averages, staff see authoring and publishing controls, at /quizzes.
A quiz can also be launched as a live poll inside a live class.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Staff: use "Build quiz"/"Build your first quiz" to open the quiz builder (Quizzes - New); use "Publish" once it is ready, or "Preview" to try it without recording an attempt.
2. Students: use "Start" to attempt a published quiz; "Review" opens the graded result once submitted.
3. Review each quiz's attempts, average score and time limit shown on its card.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A second graded attempt by the same student is refused; a preview attempt is graded but never stored.
If grading fails, the submitted answers stay on screen with "Retry grade", which resends the identical answers rather than a fresh, possibly different submission.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Only teachers/admins may build, publish or preview with an answer key; students only ever receive question text, options and points, never the answer key, until a graded result is released.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Quiz metadata and questions are read through the school adapter's quizzes resource (answer-key fields withheld from students); grading is server-side, and prior attempts are read through the quiz-attempts resource.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Quizzes - New is the quiz builder: authoring questions, options and quiz-level settings before publishing, at /quizzes/new.
Questions can be written here or pulled from the subject question bank.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Use "Add question"/"New question" to add a question, then "Add option" for each answer choice, clicking a letter to mark the correct answer.
2. Use "Bank" to pull an existing question from the subject's question bank instead of writing a new one.
3. Set quiz-level options (shuffle questions, reveal answers after submission), then "Save draft" to keep working or "Publish" to make it available to students.
4. Use "Previous"/"Next question" to move between questions while editing, and "Back" to return to the quiz list.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A question left as "Untitled question" or without a marked correct option, or without a linked subject with bank questions ("No bank questions for this subject yet."), cannot be published.
The shuffle and reveal-answers options are saved with the quiz on the server, not merely collected and discarded.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Building and publishing quizzes is limited to teachers/admins; the question bank (with answers/explanations) is only ever returned to authors, never to students.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: The quiz and its questions are saved through the school adapter's quizzes resource (with questions, shuffle, revealAnswers); bank questions come from the question-bank resource, authorized for teacher/admin only.

fields.label: Quiz title
fields.help: Shown to students on the quiz list.

fields.label: Subject
fields.help: Determines the class and question bank.

fields.label: Time limit (minutes)
fields.help: Optional time limit for an attempt.

fields.label: Reveal answers after submission
fields.help: Shows the answer key once a student submits.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Reports is the school's analytics view: attendance, admissions, academics and finance summaries, at /reports.
Every chart is computed from live data rather than a static image.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Review the available reports: school-wide attendance (last 20 school days), admissions funnel, GPA/grade distribution, collection rate by class and payment methods, among others shown on the page.
2. Use "CSV" to export a report's underlying rows, or "Print" to produce a printable version.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A report with no qualifying data for the selected period shows an explicit empty state rather than a blank chart.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Full cross-school reports are limited to admin/accountant roles consistent with the underlying statistics; other roles see only the reports relevant to their own scope.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Report figures reuse the same statistics endpoint (and its per-role derivations) that powers the Dashboard, so the two stay consistent.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Settings manages the signed-in user's own profile, notification preferences, password and active sessions within this module's own demo settings adapter, at /settings. Changing them here does not change the host application's login credentials or session.
Presentation settings (theme, density, reduced motion) are not part of this page; they go through the host's preference contract and honour tenant locks.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Review and edit profile fields (name, email, phone, language, timezone), then "Save"/"Save changes".
2. Choose how to hear about each kind of update (in-app, email, SMS) under notification preferences.
3. Use "Change password"/"Update password" with the current password and a new one (10+ characters with a capital, a number and a symbol).
4. Review "Active sessions" and use "Sign out" on any session that is no longer needed.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A new password that does not meet the stated rule, or an incorrect current password, is rejected with the server's explanation before it is changed.
Ending a session immediately revokes that session; the current session cannot be ended from this list without signing out.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: A user can only view and change their own profile, notifications, password and sessions.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Profile/notification settings, password changes and session termination are handled through the school adapter's settings resource.

fields.label: Name
fields.help: Display name shown across the module.

fields.label: Timezone
fields.help: Used to display dates and times.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Students lists the school's student directory with attendance, GPA and fee status, at /students.
A parent instead sees only their own children through the child switcher; a student sees only themselves.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Filter by class, gender, status or fee status; use "Register student" to open student registration for a new admission.
2. Open a student to review attendance, GPA, fees and contact details; use "Call guardian"/"Message guardian" to reach the recorded contact.
3. Use "Deactivate"/"Reactivate" to change a student's enrolment status.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Deactivating a student does not delete their records; historical attendance, marks and fee history remain visible.

A student's fee-status badge (Overdue/Partial/Due/Paid) and its last-payment date and method are server-computed and shown only once a payment has actually been recorded; they never reflect an assumed or pending payment.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Full directory access and status changes are limited to the admin role; a parent's view is server-scoped to their own children via the session's children list.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Students are read and patched through the school adapter's students resource; registration creates a student, where the server assigns the admission number, roll number and starting status/attendance/fee values.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Students - New is the step-by-step student registration wizard, at /students/new.
Fields marked with * are required before continuing to the next step.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Step through the wizard entering the student's name, gender, date of birth and the grade they are joining.
2. Choose a class or use "Auto-assign" to let the system place the student into a class with available seats (shown as "X of Y seats").
3. Record guardian and contact details and whether admission documents have been received.
4. Use "Back"/"Continue" to move between steps and "Register student" on the final step to submit.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A required field left blank blocks "Continue"/"Register student" with the missing fields highlighted.
The server assigns the admission number, roll number, starting status (Active), attendance (100%) and fee status (Due); the client never invents these values.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Registration is limited to the admin role.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Registration submits to the school adapter's students resource; if a class was auto-assigned or chosen, the server increments that class's strength as part of the same operation.

fields.label: Class
rules: Limited to classes with available seats.

fields.label: Documents received
fields.help: Whether admission documents have been collected.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Subjects lists core, lab and elective subjects offered per grade, at /subjects.
Each subject records its weekly period load and the department that owns it.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Filter by type (core, lab, elective) or grade; review credits and periods/week per subject.
2. Use "Add subject" to create one, entering its name, code, department, type, colour, credits and periods per week.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A duplicate subject code for the same grade is rejected before saving.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Adding or editing subjects is limited to the admin role.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Subjects are read and written through the school adapter's subjects resource; the timetable and marks pages both reference the same subject records by id.

fields.label: Subject name
fields.help: Shown across timetable, marks and report cards.

fields.label: Code
fields.help: Short subject code, for example PHY.

fields.label: Department
fields.help: Academic department the subject belongs to.

fields.label: Periods / week
fields.help: Used to build the weekly timetable.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Teachers lists the staff directory with department, employment type, rating and weekly load, at /teachers.
A teacher's own weekly timetable and home class are one click away.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Filter by department, employment type or status; use "Register teacher" to open teacher registration for a new hire.
2. Open a teacher to review their weekly timetable, home class, rating and years of experience.
3. Use "Mark on leave"/"Mark returned" to change a teacher's availability status.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Average rating and average teaching load are computed by the server from actual timetable and feedback data, not entered directly here.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Directory access and status changes are limited to the admin role.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Teachers are read and patched through the school adapter's teachers resource; registration creates a teacher, and choosing "Class teacher of" additionally updates that class's assignment.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Teachers - New is the teacher registration wizard, at /teachers/new.
It captures identity, employment and teaching-assignment details before creating the staff record.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Enter first and last name, date of birth, gender, address, department, designation and employment type.
2. Select the subjects this teacher is qualified to teach, and optionally the grades they teach.
3. Choose "Class teacher of" to make them a home-class teacher, or leave "Not a class teacher".
4. Use "Back"/"Continue" through the steps and "Register teacher" to submit.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A required identity or employment field left blank blocks continuing to the next step.
The server assigns the employee id, starting status (Active), rating (0) and weekly periods (0).

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Registration is limited to the admin role.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Registration submits to the school adapter's teachers resource; choosing a home class additionally updates that class with the new class-teacher assignment, exactly as documented in the module's API contract.

fields.label: Subjects qualified to teach
rules: At least one subject is required.

fields.label: Class teacher of
fields.help: Assigns this teacher as the home-class teacher.
rules: Leave as "Not a class teacher" when not applicable.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Timetable is the weekly class/teacher schedule grid, at /timetable.
"NOW" highlights the current period for today.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Review the weekly grid; a free period shows "Free", and a period with no assigned teacher shows "No teacher (self study)".
2. Click a period to edit it, choosing subject, teacher and room, then "Save period".
3. Review "Weekly load"/"periods / week" per teacher to check for over- or under-scheduling.
4. Use "Print" to produce a printable copy of the grid.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Assigning a teacher already teaching another class in the same period is rejected with "Clash: this teacher already teaches {class} in this period."

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Editing the timetable is limited to the admin role; teachers and students can view their own relevant slots.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: The grid is read and edited through the school adapter's timetable resource with subject/teacher/room per period.

fields.label: Teacher
rules: Cannot clash with another class in the same period.

fields.label: Room
fields.help: Room the period is held in.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Whiteboard is a standalone drawing surface reused inside a live class, at /whiteboard.
Opened outside a live session it is a local practice surface only; opened from a live class it becomes the shared teaching surface for that session.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Draw on the surface using the provided tools.
2. Use "Use in a live class" to attach the current whiteboard to an active session, or "Join a live class" to open one that already has a whiteboard shared.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Drawing performed outside a live class is never sent anywhere and is not persisted across a reload.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Sharing a whiteboard into a live class is limited to that session's host (teacher).

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: When used inside a live class, whiteboard visibility follows the same room-state actions as chat and polls; standalone use makes no network request.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The dashboard summarizes today’s appointments, encounters, pending approvals, billing queues and amounts, upcoming appointments, and low stock.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Review the summary cards and lists to identify work waiting in appointments, approvals, billing or stock. 2. Open the related destination from Healthcare Suite navigation to inspect or act on the underlying records.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Dashboard values are API results and may change after a source-backed operation. If the API is unavailable, restore connectivity and reload; this guide does not promise a cached snapshot.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host authenticates the actor and module access. The Healthcare Suite demo adapter checks tenant, product, branch, module, selected active facility and role on every request. Demo read roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst, operations, finance-manager, finance and read-only; write roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst and operations. These are demo policy roles, not a production permission model.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: The source reads GET /dashboard through the API. The demo API holds process-lifetime in-memory partitions initialized from the original CSV fixtures.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The appointment board places bookings into time slots for providers, rooms or equipment. A list view is also available.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Choose a date and resource view. 2. Select a free slot and choose a registered patient or book a guest without an MRN. 3. Confirm, reschedule by selecting another slot, mark no-show, or cancel with a reason. 4. At check-in, use Register & check in for a guest to issue an MRN.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Only free slots can be booked; the board reflects resource schedule, slot length, lunch breaks and blocks. Reschedule requires a valid new slot. Cancellation asks for a reason. API validation errors are shown by the form; retry after correcting the indicated fields.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host authenticates the actor and module access. The Healthcare Suite demo adapter checks tenant, product, branch, module, selected active facility and role on every request. Demo read roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst, operations, finance-manager, finance and read-only; write roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst and operations. These are demo policy roles, not a production permission model.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: The source uses GET /scheduling/slots and appointment create, detail, reschedule, status and register API operations. Appointment records and generated demo bookings are owned by the backend.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Patients provides searchable patient records and entry points for full or quick registration and patient preview.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Search by MRN, name, mobile, national ID or email. 2. Open a result to review its patient record or side preview. 3. Use new patient for full registration, or quick registration from a patient search box when that flow is offered. 4. Link insurance in payer, plan, TPA and network order; plan options depend on payer, and network options depend on plan.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Required values and relationship selections are validated by the API. Insurance selections are dependent: choose payer before plan and plan before network. Correct field errors and retry; do not assume an eligibility result until the API returns one.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host authenticates the actor and module access. The Healthcare Suite demo adapter checks tenant, product, branch, module, selected active facility and role on every request. Demo read roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst, operations, finance-manager, finance and read-only; write roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst and operations. These are demo policy roles, not a production permission model.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Uses GET/POST /patients, GET/PUT /patients/:id and lookup endpoints. Patient records and policy links are API-owned. The reference names and records are fictional demo data.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Encounters lists visits and provides entry points to create an encounter or open an encounter workspace.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Open an existing encounter or choose new. 2. For a new encounter, find/register a patient or select one of today’s appointments. 3. Choose department, specialty and treating provider. 4. Select cash or insurance and run the eligibility check. 5. Continue to ordering from the encounter when needed.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: An insured encounter requires an Eligible or verify-manually eligibility result from today. The consultation charge is added by the API, and a linked appointment is marked arrived. If eligibility is ineligible, review the API result and choose the available self-pay path when appropriate.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host authenticates the actor and module access. The Healthcare Suite demo adapter checks tenant, product, branch, module, selected active facility and role on every request. Demo read roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst, operations, finance-manager, finance and read-only; write roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst and operations. These are demo policy roles, not a production permission model.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Uses GET/POST /encounters, GET /encounters/:id, PATCH status, POST /eligibility/check, patient, appointment and lookup APIs. Encounter and eligibility state belongs to the API.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Approvals & eRx shows simulated prior-approval and electronic-prescription requests and their returned statuses.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Open the queue and review request state and timeline. 2. Open a request to inspect its encounter, diagnosis/justification and returned authorization status. 3. Return to the encounter ordering workflow to create or correct a request when the API reports a missing or rejected request.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Approval and eRx decisions are simulated by the demo API, including configured response delay and demo rules. A pending request is not approved. Follow the returned status and authorization number; do not treat this page as a real payer or prescribing channel.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host authenticates the actor and module access. The Healthcare Suite demo adapter checks tenant, product, branch, module, selected active facility and role on every request. Demo read roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst, operations, finance-manager, finance and read-only; write roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst and operations. These are demo policy roles, not a production permission model.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Uses GET /approvals and encounter order/approval operations. Request state and simulation are backend-owned.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Hospital billing presents encounter lines waiting for hospital invoicing, including held lines and patient-share adjustments.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Review the pending queue and select an encounter. 2. Preview the invoice lines, holds and pricing adjustments. 3. Resolve supported holds in the encounter order/approval flow, then return to billing. 4. Create an invoice and record one or more supported payment methods.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Lines may be held for pending approval or other returned API reasons. Network deductible is added once per visit and the co-pay cap applies across hospital and pharmacy billing. Confirm the preview before invoicing; payment errors leave the operation subject to API response and must be retried only after reviewing current invoice state.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host authenticates the actor and module access. The Healthcare Suite demo adapter checks tenant, product, branch, module, selected active facility and role on every request. Demo read roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst, operations, finance-manager, finance and read-only; write roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst and operations. These are demo policy roles, not a production permission model.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Uses GET /billing/pending, GET /billing/preview/:encounterId and invoice create/payment APIs. Pricing and billing state are produced by the source-backed demo API.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Pharmacy billing presents pharmacy encounter lines waiting for invoicing, including stock and eRx holds.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Review the pharmacy queue and select an encounter. 2. Inspect the preview, line holds and patient share. 3. Resolve a missing eRx or stock issue through the supported API workflow, then refresh the preview. 4. Create the invoice and record a supported payment method.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Lines can be held for an eRx that has not been sent or for out-of-stock items. An approved eRx is a demo API state and may satisfy the source approval rule for that drug. Verify current API status before invoicing; the co-pay cap is shared across hospital and pharmacy billing.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host authenticates the actor and module access. The Healthcare Suite demo adapter checks tenant, product, branch, module, selected active facility and role on every request. Demo read roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst, operations, finance-manager, finance and read-only; write roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst and operations. These are demo policy roles, not a production permission model.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Uses billing pending/preview and invoice create/payment APIs. Stock, eRx, pricing and billing state are managed by the backend demo contract.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Invoices searches and filters created invoices, with preview, print, collection, cancellation and CSV export actions.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Search or filter the invoice list. 2. Open an invoice to review and print it. 3. Collect an outstanding balance using a supported payment method. 4. Cancel only after reviewing the confirmation; cancellation returns lines to the billing queue and restores stock according to the API.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Payment requires a valid amount/method and card approval code where applicable. A cancellation changes downstream billing and stock state; verify invoice status before retrying a failed request. CSV export contains the current filtered results.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host authenticates the actor and module access. The Healthcare Suite demo adapter checks tenant, product, branch, module, selected active facility and role on every request. Demo read roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst, operations, finance-manager, finance and read-only; write roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst and operations. These are demo policy roles, not a production permission model.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Uses GET /billing/invoices, GET /billing/invoices/:id, POST payments and POST cancel. The backend owns invoice and payment state.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Payers is the worklist and editor for payer organizations used by plan, contract and eligibility demo workflows.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Search and filter by code, name, payer type or regulator ID. 2. Open a payer to inspect or edit it, or create a payer. 3. Activate or deactivate a record when its status should change.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Code, name and payer type are required; code is unique. Correct API field errors and retry. Deactivation preserves the record and may affect availability in dependent selectors.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host authenticates the actor and module access. The Healthcare Suite demo adapter checks tenant, product, branch, module, selected active facility and role on every request. Demo read roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst, operations, finance-manager, finance and read-only; write roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst and operations. These are demo policy roles, not a production permission model.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Entity metadata binds this page to the payers table and /masters/payers endpoints; lookups are API-backed. Fields include code, name, payerType, regulatorId and other source form fields.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: TPAs is the worklist and editor for third-party administrators linked from insurance plans.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Search by code, name or regulator ID. 2. Open a TPA to inspect/update it, or create a new one. 3. Change active status from the worklist when needed.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Code and name are required and code is unique. Review field errors from the API before retrying. Plans refer to a TPA, so check dependent use before deactivation.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host authenticates the actor and module access. The Healthcare Suite demo adapter checks tenant, product, branch, module, selected active facility and role on every request. Demo read roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst, operations, finance-manager, finance and read-only; write roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst and operations. These are demo policy roles, not a production permission model.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Entity metadata binds the page to the tpas table and /masters/tpas endpoints; lookup results feed plan forms. Source-required fields are code and name.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Plans stores payer insurance plans and their TPA relationship for patient policies.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Search by code, name or plan category. 2. Create a plan or open an existing plan. 3. Select the payer and TPA from API lookups, then save. 4. Use active status controls to manage whether a plan remains selectable.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Code, name, payer and TPA are required; code is unique. Select valid referenced records from lookup results. API field errors identify corrections; dependent network and patient-policy records use the plan reference.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host authenticates the actor and module access. The Healthcare Suite demo adapter checks tenant, product, branch, module, selected active facility and role on every request. Demo read roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst, operations, finance-manager, finance and read-only; write roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst and operations. These are demo policy roles, not a production permission model.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Uses /masters/insurance-plans and lookups for payers and TPAs; data maps to insurance_plans. Required source fields: code, name, payerId and tpaId.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Networks defines plan-linked coverage and pricing terms used for patient policies and billing quotes.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Search by code or name. 2. Open or create a network. 3. Select its plan and price list from API lookups and enter the network terms. 4. Save and review the resulting record.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Code, name, plan and price list are required; code is unique. Co-pay must be between 0 and 100. Network terms affect quoted patient share, deductible, cap and approval limit; confirm values with the API response before using them in a demo scenario.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host authenticates the actor and module access. The Healthcare Suite demo adapter checks tenant, product, branch, module, selected active facility and role on every request. Demo read roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst, operations, finance-manager, finance and read-only; write roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst and operations. These are demo policy roles, not a production permission model.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Uses /masters/networks, plan and price-list lookups and pricing quote operations. Source metadata validates required relationships and copayPct.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Contracts is the worklist/editor for price lists that can be linked to payers and networks.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Search by code, name or contract type. 2. Create or open a price list. 3. Enter contract type and validity dates, and select a payer where applicable. 4. Save, then open Contract pricing to edit line-level prices and coverage.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Code, name, contract type, valid-from and valid-to are required; code is unique and end date must not precede start date. Network references point to a price list, so select the intended list before configuring network terms.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host authenticates the actor and module access. The Healthcare Suite demo adapter checks tenant, product, branch, module, selected active facility and role on every request. Demo read roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst, operations, finance-manager, finance and read-only; write roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst and operations. These are demo policy roles, not a production permission model.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Uses /masters/price-lists and payer lookups; rows are stored in price_lists. Contract line editing is a separate /contracts/:priceListId/lines API workflow.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Contract pricing is an editable grid of item and service prices, coverage flags and prior-approval requirements for a selected price list.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Select/open a contract price list. 2. Review item and service lines. 3. Edit a line price and its covered/prior-approval values. 4. Save the line changes and review the returned values.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A blank contract price uses the base price less the contract default discount. Coverage and approval settings alter later quotes and billing holds. Review saved values before relying on a quote; if save fails, preserve the API error and refresh the current contract lines.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host authenticates the actor and module access. The Healthcare Suite demo adapter checks tenant, product, branch, module, selected active facility and role on every request. Demo read roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst, operations, finance-manager, finance and read-only; write roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst and operations. These are demo policy roles, not a production permission model.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Uses GET/PUT /contracts/:priceListId/lines with catalog data from /masters/items and /masters/services. The API owns contract pricing state.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Items is the stock-item catalog worklist and editor for medication and other inventory used in ordering and pharmacy billing.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Search by code, name, generic name or category. 2. Open an item or create one. 3. Enter its required catalog values, including unit of measure and base price; configure stock and eRx properties as applicable. 4. Save and manage active status from the worklist.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Code, name, category, unit of measure and base price are required; code is unique and base price cannot be negative. eRx-required products can create an approval hold in ordering. Correct API field errors before retrying.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host authenticates the actor and module access. The Healthcare Suite demo adapter checks tenant, product, branch, module, selected active facility and role on every request. Demo read roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst, operations, finance-manager, finance and read-only; write roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst and operations. These are demo policy roles, not a production permission model.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Uses /masters/items and catalog search APIs; maps to items. Source metadata validates required fields, uniqueness and nonnegative basePrice.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Services is the non-stock catalog worklist and editor for billable clinical or operational services.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Search by code, name or category. 2. Open a service or create one. 3. Enter required values and select a department where relevant. 4. Save and update active status from the worklist.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Code, name, category and base price are required; code is unique. Base price cannot be negative. Contract pricing can override coverage, price and prior-approval behavior for a service.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host authenticates the actor and module access. The Healthcare Suite demo adapter checks tenant, product, branch, module, selected active facility and role on every request. Demo read roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst, operations, finance-manager, finance and read-only; write roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst and operations. These are demo policy roles, not a production permission model.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Uses /masters/services plus department lookups and catalog search. Source metadata validates required values and stores the service in services.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Facilities is the organization worklist and editor for clinic or pharmacy locations.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Search by code, name, city or licence number. 2. Open a facility or create one. 3. Enter code, name and facility type, then save. 4. Change active status from the worklist when appropriate.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Code, name and type are required; code is unique. Facility selection is server-validated context in the host API. Check dependent departments before deactivating a facility.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host authenticates the actor and module access. The Healthcare Suite demo adapter checks tenant, product, branch, module, selected active facility and role on every request. Demo read roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst, operations, finance-manager, finance and read-only; write roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst and operations. These are demo policy roles, not a production permission model.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Uses /masters/facilities and facility lookups; maps to facilities. Required source fields are code, name and type.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Departments links an organizational unit to a facility and provides department choices to specialty, provider, service and resource forms.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Search by code, name or type. 2. Create or open a department. 3. Select its facility, then enter code, name and type. 4. Save and review its linked facility.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Code, name, facility and type are required; code is unique. Choose the facility from API lookup results. Correct field errors before retrying; dependent records use the department reference.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host authenticates the actor and module access. The Healthcare Suite demo adapter checks tenant, product, branch, module, selected active facility and role on every request. Demo read roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst, operations, finance-manager, finance and read-only; write roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst and operations. These are demo policy roles, not a production permission model.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Uses /masters/departments and facility lookups; maps facilityId to facilityName. Required source fields: code, name, facilityId and type.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Specialties manages the specialty list linked to departments and used when assigning providers and encounters.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Search by code or name. 2. Create or open a specialty. 3. Select its department and enter code and name. 4. Save and use the specialty in dependent provider/encounter workflows.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Code, name and department are required; code is unique. Choose a department from API lookups. A specialty must refer to an existing department.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host authenticates the actor and module access. The Healthcare Suite demo adapter checks tenant, product, branch, module, selected active facility and role on every request. Demo read roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst, operations, finance-manager, finance and read-only; write roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst and operations. These are demo policy roles, not a production permission model.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Uses /masters/specialties and department lookups; source metadata returns departmentName. Required source fields: code, name and departmentId.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Providers lists clinical and operational staff records that can be linked to departments, specialties and bookable resources.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Search by code, name, provider type, licence, phone or email. 2. Create or open a provider. 3. Enter code, name, provider type, gender and department; choose a specialty when applicable. 4. Save and update active status from the worklist.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Code, name, provider type, gender and department are required; code and licence number are unique. Licensed clinician types require a licence number. A supplied email must be valid. Correct API field errors before retrying.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host authenticates the actor and module access. The Healthcare Suite demo adapter checks tenant, product, branch, module, selected active facility and role on every request. Demo read roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst, operations, finance-manager, finance and read-only; write roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst and operations. These are demo policy roles, not a production permission model.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Uses /masters/providers with department and specialty lookups; provider references can populate resource forms. Source metadata enforces clinician licence and email validation.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Resources defines bookable providers, rooms, equipment and other scheduling resources linked to a department.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Search by code, name or resource type. 2. Create or open a resource. 3. Select its department and, for a provider resource, the provider it books for. 4. Save, then configure availability and blocks using the related scheduling pages.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Code, name, resource type and department are required; code is unique. Provider-type resources require a provider selection. A resource without valid schedules or outside a schedule/block may not offer an appointment slot.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host authenticates the actor and module access. The Healthcare Suite demo adapter checks tenant, product, branch, module, selected active facility and role on every request. Demo read roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst, operations, finance-manager, finance and read-only; write roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst and operations. These are demo policy roles, not a production permission model.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Uses /masters/resources with provider and department lookups; scheduling slots consume resource, schedule and block data through the API.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Availability configures a resource’s repeating schedule window, slot length and valid date range.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Search by resource or days. 2. Create or open a schedule. 3. Select a resource, days, start/end times, slot duration and validity dates. 4. Save and review the schedule as used by the appointment board.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Resource, days, times, slot minutes and valid dates are required. End time must follow start time, end date must be on or after start date, and slots must be at least five minutes. Lunch breaks and blocks also affect available slots.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host authenticates the actor and module access. The Healthcare Suite demo adapter checks tenant, product, branch, module, selected active facility and role on every request. Demo read roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst, operations, finance-manager, finance and read-only; write roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst and operations. These are demo policy roles, not a production permission model.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Uses /masters/resource-schedules with resource lookups; source validation checks time ordering, date ordering and minimum slot duration. Scheduling slots are API-generated.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Blocks & leave records unavailable intervals for a resource so appointment slots are not offered during the blocked period.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Search by resource, reason or date. 2. Create or open a block. 3. Select a resource, date, start and end times, and reason. 4. Save and confirm that the blocked interval is excluded from scheduling slots.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Resource, date, times and reason are required; end time must follow start time. Review the date and resource before saving because blocks affect booking availability.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host authenticates the actor and module access. The Healthcare Suite demo adapter checks tenant, product, branch, module, selected active facility and role on every request. Demo read roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst, operations, finance-manager, finance and read-only; write roles are enterprise-admin, admin, operations-analyst and operations. These are demo policy roles, not a production permission model.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Uses /masters/resource-blocks and resource lookups; source metadata validates time order and the scheduler consumes the stored block data.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: This Healthcare Suite workspace manages claims, payers and appeals through authenticated scoped API commands. All displayed records come from the demo API.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Choose Healthcare Suite, branch and facility. Open this RCM destination. 2. Inspect the current version, currency and records. 3. Choose Workflow action and complete its required fields. Configure ordered payer IDs against an invoice, create the next payer claim, record adjudication and retain denial appeal history. 4. Submit the action and review the updated records or error.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Money inputs use the displayed transaction currency and up to two decimal places. Commands require the latest workspace version and an operation key. A changed-key conflict or stale version does not overwrite state. Use Reload latest workspace after a version conflict. Preserve an uncertain provider operation and reconcile it before attempting another payment.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host validates tenant, product, branch, module and selected active facility. Server command capabilities govern finance, claim, configuration and review actions separately. An unavailable capability disables the action; UI state alone grants no authority. Shared effective theme, density, table and formatter preferences apply. A facility change discards the old facility form.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: The injected host transport reads GET /api/rcm/workspace and submits POST /api/rcm/commands. Durable synthetic financial partitions and provider connections are server-owned. Importing an existing invoice freezes a validated server snapshot and prevents independent source billing collection/cancellation. sections.title: Overview

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Enter at least one search criterion, then select Search. Search anywhere matches whole words, quoted phrases and exclusions; the labelled fields support partial values. More filters includes ID type, nationality, residing country, gender, date of birth and status.

Choose table or cards and open patient details inline, in a dialog, or in a drawer. Previous and next navigate the current result page. Save a named preset to the API, or reuse recent searches kept only in this workspace session. Record, booking, encounter and 360 actions retain patient identity.

sections.title: Billing corrections and shared clinical rail
paragraphs: Open Invoices & payments, then View bill for the full invoice, insurance, line totals, receipts and revision history. Edit bill changes quantities, discount, insurance authorization and notes on unpaid issued invoices. Enter a correction reason and confirm. The API recalculates using its current tariffs and retains the previous invoice snapshot. Payment history, including refunds, prevents edits. Conflicts require loading and reviewing the latest ledger before saving again. Unsaved correction values survive recoverable failures; Back to billing confirms discard.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Select a patient, convert prescriptions, add service orders, review insurance and totals, issue an invoice, then record partial or full demo payments. Open receipts and history to review changes.

Use the public typed workspace and adapters shown in TypeScript. The authenticated demo API reads patient CSV and writes a separate billing CSV ledger. Replace adapters to connect another application.
Uses effective tenant-locked preferences for layout, theme, fonts, density, tables, dates and number display. Ledger currency comes from the API and is not converted by a display preference.

Input remains on screen during recoverable errors. Retry reuses operation identity. Load the latest ledger after a conflict and review your retained input. Browser-close draft restoration is not provided.

sections.title: How to use this page

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: OP Registration keeps patient selection, registration, care and checkout in one page. Its five-step progress bar, patient strip, contextual side panels and bottom actions stay inside the existing application shell. All patient and encounter data comes from the authenticated demo API.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Search for a patient or create one using New patient. Confirm name and date of birth, review visit details, coverage and consent, then register and check in. Use the Nursing, Consultation, Orders, Billing and Checkout tabs without leaving this page. Sign the note before consultation charges post. Complete services before their charges post. Use the worklist to reopen a saved encounter.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: The server rejects missing identity and consent, duplicate active visits, stale record versions, invalid vital signs and payments above the balance. Signed notes use addenda. Pending results require an owner, due date and plan before checkout. Network retries reuse the operation ID. Saved drafts require identity and consent review again; tenant storage, retention and field exclusions apply. Reloading a conflicting record replaces the local form, so compare your values first.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Navigation access and write permission are checked by the demo API. The demo administrator can write; other authorized users can read. Effective theme, font scales, density, table settings, number/date/time formatting and language are inherited, including tenant locks. Currency comes from the ledger; formatting does not convert amounts. The five-step workflow and care tabs are fixed by this template, rather than the generic record navigation preference.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Compose RegistrationWorkspace with a RegistrationAdapter, ClinicalTemplateAdapter, authenticated scopeKey and PreferenceHost. The POST /op-registration endpoint loads configuration and executes versioned commands. Providers and services are read from CSV; encounters, appointments, payments and retry receipts share an atomic CSV snapshot scoped by tenant and application. Patient demographics reuse the existing patient API. These encounter records are separate from the older consultation and billing template stores. No real payer, payment, messaging or electronic-signature integration is connected.

paragraphs: Choose a template, paper profile, records and copies. Generate a preview, verify the identifying information, then open Print preview. Use actual size and disable browser headers. Save as PDF through the browser print dialog. Printing records a request, not confirmed physical delivery.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: The API rejects invalid records, excessive copies and labels that do not fit the paper. Reprints require permission and a reason. Retry preserves the operation identity. Payment links are synthetic; only an administrator can simulate payment status, and expired requests cannot be printed.

Your default stock does not fit this label. A compatible profile is selected for this preview; your saved default is unchanged. The tenant-locked printer stock does not fit this label. Ask your administrator to unlock it or select compatible stock.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The server isolates jobs by tenant, application and user. Tenant administrators control copy limits, reprints and locked printer profiles. Users can save an unlocked default profile. sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Compose reusable forms with shared controls, layouts, translations and rules. Designs and published answer examples use the demo API. Backend contract runtime demonstrates the supplied DCP v1 contract separately; the visual design is not a backend Dcp.Form payload.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Add fields and sections, choose presentation and label language, and preview. Dropdowns can require up to four parents; map each child option to every parent. Import CSV/XLSX into a value set, review and save its revision. Save the design, select an owner type, review, approve and publish. Compare a saved release with the current design. Published forms load owner answers and show revision history.

Select a section and enable Repeat this section to add a bounded group of rows. Set minimum and maximum rows. Each row retains its own identity, values and validation messages. Calculations run per row; changing a shared parent clears dependent selections in every row. Copying a sample remaps its internal field references. Designer repetition currently supports one row level; nested collections are available in the separate v1 runtime.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Preview checks required values, types, ranges, normalization, calculations and dropdown membership. Any parent change clears dependent selections. The v1 runtime previews edits with server rules, supports repeating rows, and keeps false as a valid present Boolean value. A 422 response displays validation errors and does not confirm a save. A conflict or uncertain save requires reviewing the server record; writes are not automatically retried.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Effective preferences and tenant locks still apply. Tenant-authored labels fall back from the selected language to English, then the original label. Shared recovery follows tenant retention and field exclusions and stores no browser-local copy. Recovery requires the same record revision and checksum. Draft Center lists DCP recovery drafts; open the designer and Backend contract runtime to review them. Masked and nonwritable v1 fields cannot be edited. Demo navigation and roles are not production field authorization.
