sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Library manages the book catalogue and issue/return/reservation workflow, at /library.
Members without an available copy can place a reservation instead of an issue.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Search and filter the catalogue by category or availability; use "Add book" to register a new title with author, ISBN, category, publisher, year, copies and shelf.
2. Use "Issue"/"Issue book" against a member for an available title, or "Renew" an existing loan (14-day loans, per the catalogue note).
3. Use "Return" to close a loan; the server computes any fine and the client shows exactly that figure.
4. When "All copies out", use the reservation action instead; the server decides whether it is filled immediately or waitlisted.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Issuing a book with no available copies is refused with "No copies available. Place a reservation instead."; issuing an unknown book id returns "Book not found".

After an issue, renewal or return, the client reloads the authoritative stock (available copies) from the server rather than adjusting it locally, so a client-side estimate cannot silently drift from the server's record.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Adding books and processing issues/returns is limited to librarian/admin roles; any registered user may request a reservation.

2. Use "Start instant class"/"Start now" to begin an unscheduled session immediately, or "Schedule" to plan one for later.
3. Use "Join lobby"/"Join now" to enter a session; a host can toggle "Recording" and see "Average attendance" after it ends.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: If a leave/end call fails, the user stays in the room rather than being silently dropped.
"Recordings stream from your media storage in production." - this reference module never stores or relays actual audio/video.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Only the assigned teacher (host) can end a session, launch/close polls, or mute/lower hands for other participants; students may raise a hand, vote and send chat messages.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Marks is the term-wise mark-entry grid and report-card source for a class, at /marks.
Entry stays open only while the term is scheduled and the paper is marked as open for entry.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Choose a class and term to load its subject columns and student rows; use the arrow keys to move between cells while entering marks.
2. Enter each student's mark per subject (within 0 and the paper's maximum), then "Save marks"; "Reset" discards unsaved edits.
3. Review "Class average", "Rank" and the grade scale (A+ >=90, A >=80, B+ >=70, B >=60, C >=50, D >=40, F) shown on the grid.
4. Use "CSV"/"Print" to export the grid, or open a student's own report card, which pulls the same marks across terms.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A mark outside 0 and the paper's maximum is rejected with "Marks must be between 0 and {max}" and highlighted as "Some marks are out of range" before saving.
A scheduled (not-yet-sat) term always returns null marks rather than a fabricated zero.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Only the class/subject teacher (or admin) may enter or edit marks for a class; students and parents only view the resulting report card.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Messages is the school's internal messaging inbox between staff, students, parents and school offices, at /messages.
Conversations are threads; opening one marks it read.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Search conversations, or use "New message" to start one, choosing a recipient from office contacts (for example the principal, school office or finance - contact labels, not separate login roles) or the teacher directory.
2. Write the message (Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line) and optionally "Attach" a file, then "Send".
3. Review the thread; a failed send keeps the draft text and any attachment so it can be retried.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: "Message not sent - {reason}" shows the exact server error and keeps the composed message on screen; "Message sent to {name}" confirms delivery.
Sending is disabled while an attachment is uploading, failed or refused.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: A user can only see and open threads they are a participant of; the server appends any reply rather than the client fabricating one.

"Notice posted to {audience}" confirms success; deleting asks "Delete “{title}”? Recipients will no longer see it." before removing it.

sections.title: Access and preferences

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Quizzes lists published and draft quizzes; students see their own attempts and averages, staff see authoring and publishing controls, at /quizzes.
A quiz can also be launched as a live poll inside a live class.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Staff: use "Build quiz"/"Build your first quiz" to open the quiz builder (Quizzes - New); use "Publish" once it is ready, or "Preview" to try it without recording an attempt.
2. Students: use "Start" to attempt a published quiz; "Review" opens the graded result once submitted.
3. Review each quiz's attempts, average score and time limit shown on its card.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A second graded attempt by the same student is refused; a preview attempt is graded but never stored.
If grading fails, the submitted answers stay on screen with "Retry grade", which resends the identical answers rather than a fresh, possibly different submission.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Only teachers/admins may build, publish or preview with an answer key; students only ever receive question text, options and points, never the answer key, until a graded result is released.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Use "Add question"/"New question" to add a question, then "Add option" for each answer choice, clicking a letter to mark the correct answer.
2. Use "Bank" to pull an existing question from the subject's question bank instead of writing a new one.
3. Set quiz-level options (shuffle questions, reveal answers after submission), then "Save draft" to keep working or "Publish" to make it available to students.
4. Use "Previous"/"Next question" to move between questions while editing, and "Back" to return to the quiz list.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A question left as "Untitled question" or without a marked correct option, or without a linked subject with bank questions ("No bank questions for this subject yet."), cannot be published.
The shuffle and reveal-answers options are saved with the quiz on the server, not merely collected and discarded.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Building and publishing quizzes is limited to teachers/admins; the question bank (with answers/explanations) is only ever returned to authors, never to students.

sections.title: Validation and recovery

sections.title: Access and preferences

sections.title: How to use this page

2. Use "Use in a live class" to attach the current whiteboard to an active session, or "Join a live class" to open one that already has a whiteboard shared.

sections.title: Access and preferences

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The dashboard summarizes today’s appointments, encounters, pending approvals, billing queues and amounts, upcoming appointments, and low stock.

sections.title: How to use this page

sections.title: Validation and recovery

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The appointment board places bookings into time slots for providers, rooms or equipment. A list view is also available.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Choose a date and resource view. 2. Select a free slot and choose a registered patient or book a guest without an MRN. 3. Confirm, reschedule by selecting another slot, mark no-show, or cancel with a reason. 4. At check-in, use Register & check in for a guest to issue an MRN.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Only free slots can be booked; the board reflects resource schedule, slot length, lunch breaks and blocks. Reschedule requires a valid new slot. Cancellation asks for a reason. API validation errors are shown by the form; retry after correcting the indicated fields.

Use new patient for full registration, or quick registration from a patient search box when that flow is offered. 4. Link insurance in payer, plan, TPA and network order; plan options depend on payer, and network options depend on plan.

paragraphs: Encounters lists visits and provides entry points to create an encounter or open an encounter workspace.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Open an existing encounter or choose new. 2. For a new encounter, find/register a patient or select one of today’s appointments. 3. Choose department, specialty and treating provider. 4. Select cash or insurance and run the eligibility check. 5. Continue to ordering from the encounter when needed.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: An insured encounter requires an Eligible or verify-manually eligibility result from today. The consultation charge is added by the API, and a linked appointment is marked arrived. If eligibility is ineligible, review the API result and choose the available self-pay path when appropriate.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Hospital billing presents encounter lines waiting for hospital invoicing, including held lines and patient-share adjustments.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Review the pending queue and select an encounter. 2. Preview the invoice lines, holds and pricing adjustments. 3. Resolve supported holds in the encounter order/approval flow, then return to billing. 4. Create an invoice and record one or more supported payment methods.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Lines may be held for pending approval or other returned API reasons. Network deductible is added once per visit and the co-pay cap applies across hospital and pharmacy billing. Confirm the preview before invoicing; payment errors leave the operation subject to API response and must be retried only after reviewing current invoice state.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Availability configures a resource’s repeating schedule window, slot length and valid date range.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Search by resource or days. 2. Create or open a schedule. 3. Select a resource, days, start/end times, slot duration and validity dates. 4. Save and review the schedule as used by the appointment board.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Resource, days, times, slot minutes and valid dates are required. End time must follow start time, end date must be on or after start date, and slots must be at least five minutes. Lunch breaks and blocks also affect available slots.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Money inputs use the displayed transaction currency and up to two decimal places. Commands require the latest workspace version and an operation key. Preserve an uncertain provider operation and reconcile it before attempting another payment.

paragraphs: Sign in, select the intended branch, select LIS1 in the header, expand navigation and select Dashboard. Wait for the API to finish loading. Source detail links remain within this module; refresh retains the route.

Source controls/text on this page include: Live position of today's work across the laboratory; Refresh; Orders today; Collected today (revenue); Open critical results; Failed instrument messages; Overdue tests; Nothing overdue; Order; Patient; Test; Status; Late by; Turnaround time, last 7 days; No signed tests yet; Department. sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A denied operation stays denied at the server even if its button is visible. Correct displayed validation errors before retrying. An unavailable service is reported as an error; no browser fixture is substituted. If a write times out, refresh and check for the record before repeating it. Unsaved form state is not a durable saved record.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The host requires authenticated module and branch access. Enterprise administrators may use source administration actions; finance managers are limited to billing mutations, and operations analysts have read-only API access. Source clinical role checks may restrict actions further. Module visibility is not a clinical privilege grant.

Shared direction, formatting, table presentation and sidebar preferences apply. Native-speaker and clinical review, source visual comparison and complete viewer, print and clinical workflow acceptance remain separate.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Requests use /reference-modules/lis1/api through the same authenticated demo API. Source service workers have separate persistent SQLite data for each tenant/application/branch and module. Login/session switching from the source app is disabled; the host supplies the actor.

No browser business fixtures are used. Source seed records, sample integration payloads and barcode generation live on the server. External socket and HTTP deliveries are disabled in this embedded demo; configure and validate real providers separately.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Today shows the patient-flow pipeline from scheduled to completed, plus the live virtual waiting room with urgent patients first, wait times, allergy flags and device status.

sections.title: Workflow
paragraphs: Review the waiting room, then use the role-aware action on the patient: a nurse selects Start triage and a doctor selects Start consult.
Use Simulate arrival to bring in the next booked demo patient, and open the consultation from that actual appointment.

sections.title: Validation
paragraphs: Start consult is offered only to the role the server allows. Nurses see Start triage and cannot start the doctor consult, and a refused action shows the server message.

sections.title: Access
paragraphs: Access comes from the trusted API role, and nurses cannot select the Doctor role. The shared header module selector and sidebar preferences replace the duplicate source sidebar.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Provider and patient modules share durable demo records scoped by tenant, application and branch. Remote video is fake and vitals, transcript, decision support and scribe output are backend simulated; only the local self-camera is real. This is not production media, a clinical claim or live RCM or insurance delivery, and no native or domain reviewer has approved it.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Schedule is a day grid per clinician with a current-time line, a date picker with previous and next day buttons, and the visit count for the day.

sections.title: Workflow
paragraphs: Pick a date and select Book visit, then choose the patient, clinician, a free slot, visit mode and reason. Select a visit block to open it, cancel it, mark no-show or restore it.

sections.title: Validation
paragraphs: Booking respects the resolved facility hours, slot interval and allowed visit modes, so occupied or out-of-hours slots cannot be chosen. A cancelled visit notifies the patient in the app.

sections.title: Access
paragraphs: Access comes from the trusted API role, and nurses cannot select the Doctor role. The shared header module selector and sidebar preferences replace the duplicate source sidebar.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Provider and patient modules share durable demo records scoped by tenant, application and branch. Remote video is fake and vitals, transcript, decision support and scribe output are backend simulated; only the local self-camera is real. This is not production media, a clinical claim or live RCM or insurance delivery, and no native or domain reviewer has approved it.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Patients lists the demo patients with search and a chart drawer showing allergies, problems and medicines.

sections.title: Workflow

sections.title: Validation
paragraphs: Registration requires identity, contact, allergy status (allergies or no known allergies) and consent. The server rejects incomplete records and its message is shown.

sections.title: Access

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Visit notes lists signed notes and open drafts and shows the selected note with a print option.

sections.title: Workflow
paragraphs: Switch between Signed and Drafts, select a patient row to read the note, and print it when needed. Continue a draft by opening its actual consultation.

sections.title: Validation
paragraphs: Signed notes are read-only and signed history is never overwritten. An empty list shows No signed notes yet or No open drafts instead of placeholder data.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Consultation is the cockpit for one actual appointment: patient banner with allergies, video stage, vitals monitor, chat and transcript, eight tabs, decision support and sign off.

sections.title: Workflow
paragraphs: Open it from Today, Schedule or Notes, never from a typed ID. A nurse completes Triage (vitals, nursing note, allergies reviewed) and selects Complete triage and hand off to doctor.
The doctor records with consent, reviews decision support, adds diagnoses, orders and prescriptions, drafts the note and selects Sign and complete visit.

sections.title: Validation
paragraphs: Doctor signing requires a primary diagnosis, reviewed allergies and critical alerts resolved or overridden with a reason. A nursing note belongs to triage and is not a universal doctor-signing requirement. Autosave and sign version conflicts preserve your draft; resolve them without overwriting signed history. Identical retried commands are idempotent, and recording always requires consent.

sections.title: Access
paragraphs: Only a doctor signs the final visit. A nurse triages and hands over, and cannot prescribe or give the final doctor signature.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Register is a three-step form: About you, Contact and Your health.

sections.title: Workflow
paragraphs: Enter first and last name, date of birth, sex and visit language, then mobile number, optional email, address, insurer, member ID and emergency contact, then allergies with severity or no known allergies, conditions, medicines, height, weight and consent.

sections.title: Validation
paragraphs: Continue needs first name, last name and date of birth, then a phone with at least 7 digits. Create account needs allergies or no known allergies, plus consent.

sections.title: Access
paragraphs: Registration is available only when the server grants canRegister. The new patient then uses only their own record and appointments.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Home shows the next visit, its live status and the right action: check in, return to the waiting room or rejoin the call.

sections.title: Workflow
paragraphs: Select the action shown on the next visit, or choose Book to schedule another one. A follow-up published after the doctor signs appears here.

sections.title: Validation
paragraphs: Only the patient's own appointments are listed, and the action always matches the visit status, so a visit that is not yet available cannot be joined.

sections.title: Access
paragraphs: Access comes from the trusted API. An ordinary patient is fixed to their own record and own appointments, and the bottom navigation of the source app is preserved.

paragraphs: Provider and patient modules share durable demo records scoped by tenant, application and branch. Remote video is fake and vitals, transcript, decision support and scribe output are backend simulated; only the local self-camera is real. This is not production media, a clinical claim or live RCM or insurance delivery, and no native or domain reviewer has approved it.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Book is a four-step flow: symptoms, clinician, time, and check and confirm.

sections.title: Workflow
paragraphs: Select symptoms, add details and a severity from 0 to 10, pick a specialty and clinician, choose a day, a free time and Video, Phone or Chat, then select Confirm booking.

sections.title: Validation
paragraphs: Step one needs a symptom or details longer than three characters. Wait for current demo advice from the API before continuing; changed answers cancel older advice, and failed advice offers a retry. Urgency and specialty suggestions are simulated, not medical advice. Available times and visit modes follow the adopted branch policy; an occupied slot shows the server error.

sections.title: Access
paragraphs: Access comes from the trusted API. An ordinary patient is fixed to their own record and own appointments, and the bottom navigation of the source app is preserved.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: My health lists allergies, medicines, conditions, devices and past visit summaries for the signed-in patient.

sections.title: Workflow
paragraphs: Review each section and open a past summary from the visit list.

sections.title: Validation
paragraphs: Only the signed-in patient's own record is shown, and summaries appear only after the doctor signs. A missing or unauthorized record shows an error instead of another patient's data.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Visit covers check-in, the waiting room and the call screen for one appointment.

sections.title: Workflow
paragraphs: Open it from Home for the actual appointment. Answer the questions, run the camera, microphone and connection test, set device sharing and recording consent, then select Join the waiting room.
When the clinician is ready, join the call and use mute, camera, chat and leave.

sections.title: Validation
paragraphs: Joining needs the completed questionnaire and device check, and the server mandates recording consent. The self-camera is real but the clinician's video is fake.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Visit summary is the printable plain-language result: what we found, medicines, tests and referrals, nurse follow-up, follow-up visit and fit note.

sections.title: Workflow
paragraphs: Open it from Home or My health after the doctor signs, read each section and print it if needed.

sections.title: Validation
paragraphs: The summary is available only after signing and only for the selected patient’s own appointment. An unsigned visit displays a waiting message while the summary is checked again; a forbidden record cannot be read. Printing uses the shared document surface and includes the synthetic-demo disclaimer.

paragraphs: Search for a patient or create one using New patient. Confirm name and date of birth, review visit details, coverage and consent, then register and check in. sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: The server rejects missing identity and consent, duplicate active visits, stale record versions, invalid vital signs and payments above the balance. Signed notes use addenda. Pending results require an owner, due date and plan before checkout. Network retries reuse the operation ID. Saved drafts require identity and consent review again; tenant storage, retention and field exclusions apply. Reloading a conflicting record replaces the local form, so compare your values first.

sections.title: Access and preferences

paragraphs: The API rejects invalid records, excessive copies and labels that do not fit the paper. Reprints require permission and a reason. Retry preserves the operation identity. sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Compose reusable forms with shared controls, layouts, translations and rules. Designs and published answer examples use the demo API. Backend contract runtime demonstrates the supplied DCP v1 contract separately; the visual design is not a backend Dcp.Form payload.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Add fields and sections, choose presentation and label language, and preview. Dropdowns can require up to four parents; map each child option to every parent. Import CSV/XLSX into a value set, review and save its revision. Save the design, select an owner type, review, approve and publish. Compare a saved release with the current design. Published forms load owner answers and show revision history.

Select a section and enable Repeat this section to add a bounded group of rows. Set minimum and maximum rows. Each row retains its own identity, values and validation messages. Calculations run per row; changing a shared parent clears dependent selections in every row. Copying a sample remaps its internal field references. Designer repetition currently supports one row level; nested collections are available in the separate v1 runtime.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Preview checks required values, types, ranges, normalization, calculations and dropdown membership. Any parent change clears dependent selections. The v1 runtime previews edits with server rules, supports repeating rows, and keeps false as a valid present Boolean value. A 422 response displays validation errors and does not confirm a save. A conflict or uncertain save requires reviewing the server record; writes are not automatically retried.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Effective preferences and tenant locks still apply. Tenant-authored labels fall back from the selected language to English, then the original label. Shared recovery follows tenant retention and field exclusions and stores no browser-local copy. Recovery requires the same record revision and checksum. Draft Center lists DCP recovery drafts; open the designer and Backend contract runtime to review them. Masked and nonwritable v1 fields cannot be edited. Demo navigation and roles are not production field authorization.

With an empty menu search, Escape also closes it and returns focus to the toggle. The header remains accessible while the sidebar is open. A managed pinned sidebar stays open.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Use DcpDesignerWorkspace for frontend authoring and DcpHostRuntime with createDcpRuntimeAdapter for host-bound v1 forms. The application supplies authenticated load, preview and save routes, scope identity and optional shared recovery scope. Revisions remain strings; collection rows use _id; omitted values retain data and null clears explicitly. Jira PLIBRYBEND-206 contains the verified backend handoff and remaining backend work. Advanced enterprise contracts and actual production/native acceptance are not yet complete.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Overview is the Lumen Reports landing page, shown at the module's root route ( / ). It greets the signed-in user and surfaces reports they have already run or starred, background jobs and upcoming email schedules.
Every list on this page is already scoped to the current user's role and branch access; nothing on this page is configured locally.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Read the header greeting ("Good morning/afternoon/evening, {name}") and use "Open report library" to browse all reports, or "Build a report" (only shown when the role may create custom reports) to start a new one.
2. Review "Recently run" and "Favorites": each entry links straight to that report's viewer. Star a report from the library to have it appear under Favorites here.
3. Check "Background reports": long-running or exported runs appear here with their status; "All my reports" opens the full My reports list.

4. Review "Your access" for the current role's report count, branch scope and whether sensitive columns are masked, and "Upcoming schedules" for the next scheduled email deliveries, with a link to manage them.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: If the URL includes ?denied=1 (redirected from a page the role cannot open), a warning notice explains that the page needs a permission the role does not have.
Recent/favorite/job/schedule lists render their own empty states when there is no data yet; there is no separate error state on this page beyond the shared page-load retry.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Visible content depends on the signed-in role's report grants (view/export/email/schedule/BI) resolved on the server; "Build a report" only appears when the role may create custom reports.
Dates, times and counts use the organisation's timezone and the viewer's own number/date format preferences.

sections.title: Integration

Every link (report, job, schedule) carries the source's own identifier so the destination page resolves the exact same record.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The report library lists every report definition the signed-in role may view, with its category, title and description, at the module route /reports.
Selecting a report opens the report viewer, which runs it against the caller's own access, branch scope and masking rules.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Use the search box and category filter to narrow the list; the current query is kept in the ?q= URL parameter so a filtered view can be shared or reopened.
2. Star a report to pin it to Favorites on the Overview page; unstar the same way.
3. Open a report to reach the viewer, where filters, sorting, columns and the period can be adjusted, then run it on screen, in the background, or schedule it for email delivery.

4. In the viewer, use "Columns" to add optional fields (locked columns contain sensitive data and stay masked for roles without unmask access) and "Save view" to keep a filter/column layout for next time.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: If a report link is opened without access, the library redirects back with ?denied=1 and a notice explaining that an administrator must grant it.
A period longer than the report's on-screen limit is refused with an explanation to use "Run in background" instead; export/print/email actions not permitted for the role are not offered.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The reports and columns available, and whether values are masked, come from the role's grants and branch scope; local UI state cannot add access to a report or column.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Roles and access decides, per role, which reports can be viewed, exported, emailed, scheduled or pulled by BI tools, at /admin/access.
Every screen, export, schedule, email request and API call checks these rules on the server, not just this screen.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Select a role to review its permissions (features) and, below, its per-report grants (view/export/email/schedule/BI) and any branch or masking limits.
2. Use "New role"/"Create role" to add a role, and "Delete role" to remove one that is no longer needed.
3. Toggle the grants for each report against the selected role, then "Save access" to persist the change.
4. Review user counts per role before deleting one, since removing a role removes those grants from every user holding it.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Administrators always have every permission and every report, so that grant set cannot be edited away.
Saving an invalid combination (for example a grant with no matching report) is rejected before the change is applied.

sections.title: Access and preferences

sections.title: Validation and recovery

SMTP settings here select a delivery mode for the synthetic outbox; configuring them does not connect an actual mail provider in this demo, and every attempted message is recorded in the outbox instead of being sent.

paragraphs: API keys and BI gives dashboards and spreadsheets read-only access to the reports the issuing user is allowed to see, at /api-keys.
A key acts as its owner: the same reports, branches and masking apply as when that person signs in.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Review existing keys and the reports each may pull; use "Create key" to issue a new one (only shown when the role may create keys).
2. Copy the generated key immediately - "Copy this key now. It will not be shown again."

3. Connect a BI tool using the shown base URL and key, following the tool-specific note (for example Power BI/Excel via Get data, From Web, with an Authorization: Bearer header, or Tableau's Web Data Connector).
4. Use "Revoke"/"Revoke key" to disable a key immediately once it is no longer needed.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Only reports with the API/BI action granted to that role are ever listed as pullable by a key; a revoked key stops working immediately on its next request.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Key creation is limited to roles allowed to create API keys; a key can never see more reports, branches or unmasked columns than its owner's own role.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Report builder lists every custom report definition the signed-in user may see, and opens a builder for a new or existing one, at /builder.

Custom reports are built from approved datasets (for example revenue, claims or admissions); in this reference demo the dataset content is synthetic, and a production deployment is expected to connect its own approved read-only data source rather than a live transactional database.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. From the list, review each report's dataset, visibility (private, shared with roles, or everyone) and owner (administrators only see the owner column), then "Edit" or delete it.
2. Select "New report" to start one: choose a dataset, then add grouping, measures and calculated columns; a preview of the results is shown before saving.
3. Use "Add measure" and "Add calculated column" to extend the report, "Refresh preview" to re-run it against the current definition, and "Reset" to discard unsaved changes.
4. Set the report's visibility and, for shared reports, the roles allowed to see it, then save; existing saved views and schedules that reference the report keep working after an edit.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Saving validates the definition against the selected dataset; an invalid grouping, measure or calculated column is rejected with the specific error before the save completes.
Deleting a definition asks for confirmation naming the report; access, branch limits and masking continue to apply to anyone the report is shared with.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Only roles with report-build access see "New report"/"Edit"; the owner column and cross-user visibility are limited to administrators.
Shared/everyone visibility does not bypass a viewer's own report, branch or column-masking grants.

sections.title: How to use this page

2. Use "New dashboard" (only shown when the role may create dashboards) to start one; it opens private and empty.
3. Inside a dashboard, use "Edit" then "Add widget" to attach reports, and "Save dashboard" to persist the layout; "Delete dashboard" removes it entirely.
4. Use the sharing controls to change visibility and, for shared dashboards, the roles who may view it.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A widget backed by a report the current viewer cannot access is not shown to that viewer, even though it may be visible to others on a shared dashboard.
Deleting a dashboard asks for confirmation before removing it for every viewer it was shared with.

sections.title: Access and preferences

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Email requests lets registered users receive a report by emailing the reports mailbox, at /email-in.
Requests from unknown or unverified senders are dropped without a reply.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Review "How to request a report by email" for the accepted message format and the reports mailbox address.
2. Use "Try it here"/"Send test email" to simulate an incoming email; it runs the same processing as a real inbound message and any reply appears in the email outbox.
3. Review the inbound log entries below to confirm which requests were processed, and their result.
4. Administrators can turn the whole feature on or off from this page; while off, incoming requests are not processed.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: An unrecognised or unverified sender is dropped silently, with no reply and no log entry treated as processed.
Results are only ever sent back to the original sender, with that sender's own role, branches and masking applied - never to an address named in the message body.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Turning the feature on/off is limited to administrators; any registered user may send a request once it is enabled.

paragraphs: The simulated inbound message and its processing go through the reports adapter's email-in endpoint; delivery is recorded in the same outbox used by scheduled and job-based email.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: My reports (Jobs) lists background report runs: long periods, large exports and scheduled/emailed deliveries, at /jobs.
Opening a job shows its full detail, including delivery result and, while it is queued or running, its live progress.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Review the jobs table for status (queued, running, completed, failed), report title and requested time; open a row for its detail.
2. On the detail page, review status, filters used, format, row count, file size, delivery method (email or download) and the actual delivery result.
3. While a job is queued or running, the page automatically re-reads it every 2.5 seconds until it finishes; no manual reload is required to see completion.
4. Once finished, use the offered download or check the reported email delivery result; results are kept only for the retention period shown on the list header.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A failed job shows its server-reported error text directly on the detail page.
Only up to the configured maximum number of active jobs per user may run at once; a job past its retention window is removed and can no longer be downloaded.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Administrators can see every user's jobs from this list; other roles see only their own.

paragraphs: Job status, results and retention come from the reports adapter's jobs endpoints via the injected host adapter; the detail page polls the same adapter rather than a client-side timer with fabricated progress.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Schedules lists reports delivered by email on a timetable, at /schedules.

Each run covers a moving period (for example "last full month"); the server deduplicates a scheduled occurrence against its in-memory run record so a due occurrence is not processed twice in the same demo session, which is not the same as a durable, crash-safe delivery guarantee.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Review existing schedules and their next occurrences; use "New schedule"/"Create schedule" to add one, choosing a report, recipients and timing.
2. Use "Run now" to trigger an individual schedule immediately, or, for administrators, "Process due schedules now" to run every schedule currently due.
3. Use the delete action to remove a schedule; it stops future occurrences without affecting runs already delivered.
4. If no schedules exist yet, use "Create one here, or open any report and choose Schedule" from the report viewer instead.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Creating a schedule requires a report the role may schedule and at least one recipient; an invalid timing expression is rejected with the shown explanation before saving.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: A schedule can only be created for reports the current role is granted to schedule; "Process due schedules now" is limited to administrators.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Dashboard shows the role-specific home screen for the signed-in school user (admin, teacher, student, parent, librarian or accountant), at /dashboard.
Each portal surfaces only the statistics and shortcuts relevant to that role; a parent sees only their own children's cards, not the whole school.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Sign in through the host and choose an available School view in the header. The server confirms that your account may use the selected role before loading its dashboard.

2. Review the role's headline metrics (for example admin: attendance and collections; teacher: today's schedule and pending grading; student: schedule, attendance and open assignments; librarian: issues, overdues and stock; accountant: billed/collected/outstanding).
3. Use the dashboard shortcuts to jump into the relevant page (attendance, assignments, fees, library and so on).
4. A parent uses the child switcher to move between their own children's cards; each card reloads that child's own statistics.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: If the initial lookups (school calendar, profile, classes, subjects or teachers) fail to load, the module shows an error state with retry instead of a broken dashboard.
A trend figure (for example an attendance or collections change) is shown only when the server actually returns one; the client never invents a trend.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The server resolves and confirms the authenticated user's role; an unconfirmed or unknown role is never treated as admin, and the client shows an access state instead of a portal in that case.
A parent's requests are scoped to their own children only; the server enforces that ownership.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: The header selects a School view; it does not grant permissions. The session endpoint confirms the effective role from authenticated server entitlements, and every School request carries the selected module for server validation. Other browser tabs keep their own selected view.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Admissions tracks prospective students through the enrolment funnel, from applied to enrolled, at /admissions.
Applications are shown as cards on a stage board; the applicant's parent contact stays visible at every stage.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Review the funnel counts (applications, conversion) and the board of applications grouped by stage.
2. Use "New application"/"Create application" to add one, entering the applicant's name and the grade they are applying for.
3. Advance an application by dragging its card to the next stage, or use the stage arrows; "Advance to" shows the next available stage.
4. Use "Decline" to close an application, or "Enrol & register" once an application reaches its final stage, which continues into student registration.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: An application dropped on an invalid stage, or an incomplete new application, is rejected before the stage change or creation is saved.
"Application {id} created" confirms a successful save; a failed request keeps the entered values so the form can be retried.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Assignments lets teachers set and grade class work, and lets students turn it in, at /assignments.
The page adapts to role: teachers see class averages and grading progress; students see what is due and their own submission state.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Teachers: use "New assignment" to create one, then "Publish" to make it visible to the class (or "Save draft" to hold it back); "Close submissions"/"Reopen" controls whether students can still submit.
2. Teachers: open a submission to grade it, entering marks (0 to the assignment's maximum) and optional feedback; "No work received" marks ungraded, unsubmitted work.
3. Students: open an assignment due and use "Submit"/"Turn in" with the answer text and any attachment; a submission after the due date is recorded as late.
4. Both roles can track progress from the class-average and "Overdue"/"Due" indicators on the list.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Marks outside 0 to the assignment's maximum are rejected with "Marks must be between 0 and {max}" before the grade is saved.
Saving, turning in or sending is disabled while an attachment is uploading, failed or refused; a failed upload keeps the file selected so "Retry upload" can resend the identical payload.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Only the assigned class's teacher may publish, close or grade an assignment; a student may only submit to their own class's assignments.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Attendance records daily class presence and lets students/parents request leave, at /attendance.
A teacher marks a whole class register for a date; students and parents instead see that student's own attendance history.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Teachers: pick a class and date, mark each student Present/Absent/Late/Excused (a missing mark defaults to Present), then "Save register".
2. Teachers: use "All present" to mark the whole class present in one step, and "Reset" to discard unsaved changes to the register.
3. Students/parents: review the attendance calendar and the last-60-day summary (present/absent/late/excused), and use "Submit request" to send a leave request with a date range and reason.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A register cannot be saved with an invalid payload; the server rejects an incomplete request before any row is stored.
"Register saved" confirms a successful save; weekends and future dates never accept a status and show as such on the calendar.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Only the class's own teacher may mark or edit that class's register; a parent can only submit leave requests and view attendance for their own children.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Calendar shows the school's month view of scheduled events, at /calendar.
Events are shown alongside the same term structure already used by exams and reports.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Use "Previous month"/"Next month" (or "Today") to navigate; "Coming up" lists the next events regardless of the month shown.
2. Use "Add event"/"Add calendar event" to create one, entering title, type, location, start and (optionally, for multi-day events) end.
3. Use "Export" to download the calendar for use in an external calendar application.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: An event with a start after its end (for multi-day events) is rejected before saving.
A day with more events than fit shows a "+N more" indicator rather than silently hiding them.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Creating events is limited to the admin role; every role can view the calendar.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Classes lists the school's class/sections with their strength, class teacher and average score, at /classes.
Each class links to its own attendance register, mark list and timetable.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Review the class list, including occupancy (% seats filled), class teacher, GPA and gender split.
2. Use "Add class"/"Create class" to add a section, entering grade, section, name, room, capacity, stream and class teacher.
3. From a class, jump to its "Attendance", "Mark list" or "Timetable" using the shown shortcuts.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Creating a class requires grade, section and a capacity greater than zero; the server initializes its strength and average score at zero.
A class teacher can only be assigned from the teacher directory; an invalid selection is rejected before saving.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Creating or editing classes is limited to the admin role.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Exams schedules terms and papers and shows admit-card/day-of information, at /exams.
Students see their own schedule and checklist; staff see the scheduling and invigilation view.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Staff: use "Schedule paper"/"Schedule" to set a subject, date, time and room for a term's paper.
2. Students: review "Next paper" and the full schedule, then use "Print admit card" before the exam.

3. Review the "Exam-day checklist" (arrive 15 minutes early with admit card and ID; only transparent pencil cases and approved calculators; phones handed to the invigilator) and, for staff, "My duties" for invigilation assignments.
4. After marking, review the "Mark list" for a paper, and "Max"/"Marked" counts to track completion.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Scheduling a paper for a subject/date/room already in use for that class is rejected as a clash before saving.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Scheduling papers and viewing full invigilation duties is limited to the teacher and admin roles; students see only their own class's published schedule.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Fees manages student invoices and payment collection for finance staff, and shows a family's own balance for students/parents, at /fees.
Payment actions record synthetic payment information through the API; they never create a live bank or payment-provider transaction.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Finance staff: filter by class/term/status, then open an invoice and use "Collect"/"Collect payment" to record an amount and method.
2. Finance staff: use "Remind all" to send payment reminders by email/SMS to every family with an outstanding invoice in the current filter.
3. Students/parents: review "Balance due"/"Paid" for each invoice and the sibling-discount and late-fee policy shown on the page.
4. Use "Print" to produce a receipt/statement for a settled or partial invoice.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: An amount greater than the invoice's outstanding balance is rejected by the server rather than silently capped; an amount of zero is a no-op. A successful payment returns the server-issued status (Paid/Partial) and, when actually generated, a receipt number; the client never invents a receipt number or claims an email was sent unless the server reports it.
The student's overall fee status (Overdue > Partial > Due > Paid) is recomputed by the server after every payment, not calculated locally.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Recording payments and sending reminders is limited to the accountant and admin roles; students and parents can only view their own (or their child's) invoices.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Library manages the book catalogue and issue/return/reservation workflow, at /library.
Members without an available copy can place a reservation instead of an issue.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Search and filter the catalogue by category or availability; use "Add book" to register a new title with author, ISBN, category, publisher, year, copies and shelf.
2. Use "Issue"/"Issue book" against a member for an available title, or "Renew" an existing loan (14-day loans, per the catalogue note).
3. Use "Return" to close a loan; the server computes any fine and the client shows exactly that figure.
4. When "All copies out", use the reservation action instead; the server decides whether it is filled immediately or waitlisted.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Issuing a book with no available copies is refused with "No copies available. Place a reservation instead."; issuing an unknown book id returns "Book not found".

After an issue, renewal or return, the client reloads the authoritative stock (available copies) from the server rather than adjusting it locally, so a client-side estimate cannot silently drift from the server's record.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Adding books and processing issues/returns is limited to librarian/admin roles; any registered user may request a reservation.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Live lists scheduled, in-progress and ended live classes, at /live.
Selecting a live or upcoming session opens the live-room; recording, chat and polls exchange state through the API only, and no audio or video leaves the browser in this reference module.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Review sessions by status (Scheduled/Live/Ended), computed from each session's start time and duration against the server clock.
2. Use "Start instant class"/"Start now" to begin an unscheduled session immediately, or "Schedule" to plan one for later.
3. Use "Join lobby"/"Join now" to enter a session; a host can toggle "Recording" and see "Average attendance" after it ends.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: If a leave/end call fails, the user stays in the room rather than being silently dropped.
"Recordings stream from your media storage in production." - this reference module never stores or relays actual audio/video.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Only the assigned teacher (host) can end a session, launch/close polls, or mute/lower hands for other participants; students may raise a hand, vote and send chat messages.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Marks is the term-wise mark-entry grid and report-card source for a class, at /marks.
Entry stays open only while the term is scheduled and the paper is marked as open for entry.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Choose a class and term to load its subject columns and student rows; use the arrow keys to move between cells while entering marks.
2. Enter each student's mark per subject (within 0 and the paper's maximum), then "Save marks"; "Reset" discards unsaved edits.
3. Review "Class average", "Rank" and the grade scale (A+ >=90, A >=80, B+ >=70, B >=60, C >=50, D >=40, F) shown on the grid.
4. Use "CSV"/"Print" to export the grid, or open a student's own report card, which pulls the same marks across terms.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A mark outside 0 and the paper's maximum is rejected with "Marks must be between 0 and {max}" and highlighted as "Some marks are out of range" before saving.
A scheduled (not-yet-sat) term always returns null marks rather than a fabricated zero.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Only the class/subject teacher (or admin) may enter or edit marks for a class; students and parents only view the resulting report card.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Messages is the school's internal messaging inbox between staff, students, parents and school offices, at /messages.
Conversations are threads; opening one marks it read.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Search conversations, or use "New message" to start one, choosing a recipient from office contacts (for example the principal, school office or finance - contact labels, not separate login roles) or the teacher directory.
2. Write the message (Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line) and optionally "Attach" a file, then "Send".
3. Review the thread; a failed send keeps the draft text and any attachment so it can be retried.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: "Message not sent - {reason}" shows the exact server error and keeps the composed message on screen; "Message sent to {name}" confirms delivery.
Sending is disabled while an attachment is uploading, failed or refused.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: A user can only see and open threads they are a participant of; the server appends any reply rather than the client fabricating one.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Notices posts school-wide or audience-targeted announcements, at /notices.
A pinned notice stays at the top of the list for its audience.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Review notices, newest first, with pinned ones at the top; use "Pin"/"Pin to top" or unpin as needed.
2. Use "Post notice"/"Post a notice" to add one, choosing the audience and writing the message (at least 10 characters).
3. Use "Delete" to remove a notice; the confirmation states that recipients will no longer see it.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A message under 10 characters is rejected before posting.
"Notice posted to {audience}" confirms success; deleting asks "Delete “{title}”? Recipients will no longer see it." before removing it.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Posting, pinning and deleting notices is limited to the admin and teacher roles; the audience selector controls who receives it, enforced server-side.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Quizzes lists published and draft quizzes; students see their own attempts and averages, staff see authoring and publishing controls, at /quizzes.
A quiz can also be launched as a live poll inside a live class.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Staff: use "Build quiz"/"Build your first quiz" to open the quiz builder (Quizzes - New); use "Publish" once it is ready, or "Preview" to try it without recording an attempt.
2. Students: use "Start" to attempt a published quiz; "Review" opens the graded result once submitted.
3. Review each quiz's attempts, average score and time limit shown on its card.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A second graded attempt by the same student is refused; a preview attempt is graded but never stored.
If grading fails, the submitted answers stay on screen with "Retry grade", which resends the identical answers rather than a fresh, possibly different submission.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Only teachers/admins may build, publish or preview with an answer key; students only ever receive question text, options and points, never the answer key, until a graded result is released.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Quizzes - New is the quiz builder: authoring questions, options and quiz-level settings before publishing, at /quizzes/new.
Questions can be written here or pulled from the subject question bank.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Use "Add question"/"New question" to add a question, then "Add option" for each answer choice, clicking a letter to mark the correct answer.
2. Use "Bank" to pull an existing question from the subject's question bank instead of writing a new one.
3. Set quiz-level options (shuffle questions, reveal answers after submission), then "Save draft" to keep working or "Publish" to make it available to students.
4. Use "Previous"/"Next question" to move between questions while editing, and "Back" to return to the quiz list.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A question left as "Untitled question" or without a marked correct option, or without a linked subject with bank questions ("No bank questions for this subject yet."), cannot be published.
The shuffle and reveal-answers options are saved with the quiz on the server, not merely collected and discarded.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Building and publishing quizzes is limited to teachers/admins; the question bank (with answers/explanations) is only ever returned to authors, never to students.

sections.title: Access and preferences

paragraphs: Settings manages the signed-in user's own profile, notification preferences, password and active sessions within this module's own demo settings adapter, at /settings. Changing them here does not change the host application's login credentials or session.

2. Choose how to hear about each kind of update (in-app, email, SMS) under notification preferences.
3. Use "Change password"/"Update password" with the current password and a new one (10+ characters with a capital, a number and a symbol).
4. Review "Active sessions" and use "Sign out" on any session that is no longer needed.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A new password that does not meet the stated rule, or an incorrect current password, is rejected with the server's explanation before it is changed.
Ending a session immediately revokes that session; the current session cannot be ended from this list without signing out.

sections.title: Access and preferences

3. Use "Deactivate"/"Reactivate" to change a student's enrolment status.

A student's fee-status badge (Overdue/Partial/Due/Paid) and its last-payment date and method are server-computed and shown only once a payment has actually been recorded; they never reflect an assumed or pending payment.

paragraphs: Teachers lists the staff directory with department, employment type, rating and weekly load, at /teachers.

sections.title: Overview

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Today shows the patient-flow pipeline from scheduled to completed, plus the live virtual waiting room with urgent patients first, wait times, allergy flags and device status.

sections.title: Workflow
paragraphs: Review the waiting room, then use the role-aware action on the patient: a nurse selects Start triage and a doctor selects Start consult.
Use Simulate arrival to bring in the next booked demo patient, and open the consultation from that actual appointment.

sections.title: Validation
paragraphs: Start consult is offered only to the role the server allows. Nurses see Start triage and cannot start the doctor consult, and a refused action shows the server message.

sections.title: Access
paragraphs: Access comes from the trusted API role, and nurses cannot select the Doctor role. The shared header module selector and sidebar preferences replace the duplicate source sidebar.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Provider and patient modules share durable demo records scoped by tenant, application and branch. Remote video is fake and vitals, transcript, decision support and scribe output are backend simulated; only the local self-camera is real. This is not production media, a clinical claim or live RCM or insurance delivery, and no native or domain reviewer has approved it.

sections.title: Workflow

paragraphs: Open it from Today, Schedule or Notes, never from a typed ID. A nurse completes Triage (vitals, nursing note, allergies reviewed) and selects Complete triage and hand off to doctor.

Identical retried commands are idempotent, and recording always requires consent.

Version 2 adds structured medication, laboratory, imaging and procedure order dialogs. All entered order details are saved by the API. Cancellation retains the original order in history.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Save draft writes an explicit API record. Restore uses the saved-record selector. Failed requests preserve entered values; retry keeps the same operation ID. Reload after a conflict replaces unsaved edits only after confirmation.
Confirm identity and consent review before completing this action.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Inject createCareAdapter and the effective preference host into CareWorkspace. The authenticated POST /care-pages endpoint scopes saved records by tenant, application, user and page. Definitions and synthetic patients and beds come from backend JSON and CSV files.

This is a reusable frontend demonstration, not a production clinical system. Payer verification, physical transfers, bed cleaning, real prescriptions and legally validated signatures require separate integrations. Do not enter real patient data.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Compose reusable forms with shared controls, layouts, translations and rules. Designs and published answer examples use the demo API. Backend contract runtime demonstrates the supplied DCP v1 contract separately; the visual design is not a backend Dcp.Form payload.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Add fields and sections, choose presentation and label language, and preview. Dropdowns can require up to four parents; map each child option to every parent. Import CSV/XLSX into a value set, review and save its revision. Save the design, select an owner type, review, approve and publish. Compare a saved release with the current design. Published forms load owner answers and show revision history.

Select a section and enable Repeat this section to add a bounded group of rows. Set minimum and maximum rows. Each row retains its own identity, values and validation messages. Calculations run per row; changing a shared parent clears dependent selections in every row. Copying a sample remaps its internal field references. Designer repetition currently supports one row level; nested collections are available in the separate v1 runtime.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Preview checks required values, types, ranges, normalization, calculations and dropdown membership. Any parent change clears dependent selections. The v1 runtime previews edits with server rules, supports repeating rows, and keeps false as a valid present Boolean value. A 422 response displays validation errors and does not confirm a save. A conflict or uncertain save requires reviewing the server record; writes are not automatically retried.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Effective preferences and tenant locks still apply. Tenant-authored labels fall back from the selected language to English, then the original label. Shared recovery follows tenant retention and field exclusions and stores no browser-local copy. Recovery requires the same record revision and checksum. Draft Center lists DCP recovery drafts; open the designer and Backend contract runtime to review them. Masked and nonwritable v1 fields cannot be edited. Demo navigation and roles are not production field authorization.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: Use DcpDesignerWorkspace for frontend authoring and DcpHostRuntime with createDcpRuntimeAdapter for host-bound v1 forms. The application supplies authenticated load, preview and save routes, scope identity and optional shared recovery scope. Revisions remain strings; collection rows use _id; omitted values retain data and null clears explicitly. Jira PLIBRYBEND-206 contains the verified backend handoff and remaining backend work. Advanced enterprise contracts and actual production/native acceptance are not yet complete.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Overview is the Lumen Reports landing page, shown at the module's root route ( / ). It greets the signed-in user and surfaces reports they have already run or starred, background jobs and upcoming email schedules.
Every list on this page is already scoped to the current user's role and branch access; nothing on this page is configured locally.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Read the header greeting ("Good morning/afternoon/evening, {name}") and use "Open report library" to browse all reports, or "Build a report" (only shown when the role may create custom reports) to start a new one.
2. Review "Recently run" and "Favorites": each entry links straight to that report's viewer. Star a report from the library to have it appear under Favorites here.
3. Check "Background reports": long-running or exported runs appear here with their status; "All my reports" opens the full My reports list.

4. Review "Your access" for the current role's report count, branch scope and whether sensitive columns are masked, and "Upcoming schedules" for the next scheduled email deliveries, with a link to manage them.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: If the URL includes ?denied=1 (redirected from a page the role cannot open), a warning notice explains that the page needs a permission the role does not have.
Recent/favorite/job/schedule lists render their own empty states when there is no data yet; there is no separate error state on this page beyond the shared page-load retry.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Visible content depends on the signed-in role's report grants (view/export/email/schedule/BI) resolved on the server; "Build a report" only appears when the role may create custom reports.
Dates, times and counts use the organisation's timezone and the viewer's own number/date format preferences.

An unpinned sidebar follows the effective hover or click setting. Its navigation button toggles it. Choosing a menu page or clicking outside closes it. With an empty menu search, Escape also closes it and returns focus to the toggle. The header remains accessible while the sidebar is open. A managed pinned sidebar stays open.

sections.title: Integration
paragraphs: The page loads through the reports adapter's overview loader via the injected module host adapter; it never queries a database directly.
Every link (report, job, schedule) carries the source's own identifier so the destination page resolves the exact same record.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The report library lists every report definition the signed-in role may view, with its category, title and description, at the module route /reports.
Selecting a report opens the report viewer, which runs it against the caller's own access, branch scope and masking rules.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Use the search box and category filter to narrow the list; the current query is kept in the ?q= URL parameter so a filtered view can be shared or reopened.
2. Star a report to pin it to Favorites on the Overview page; unstar the same way.
3. Open a report to reach the viewer, where filters, sorting, columns and the period can be adjusted, then run it on screen, in the background, or schedule it for email delivery.

4. In the viewer, use "Columns" to add optional fields (locked columns contain sensitive data and stay masked for roles without unmask access) and "Save view" to keep a filter/column layout for next time.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: If a report link is opened without access, the library redirects back with ?denied=1 and a notice explaining that an administrator must grant it.
A period longer than the report's on-screen limit is refused with an explanation to use "Run in background" instead; export/print/email actions not permitted for the role are not offered.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: The reports and columns available, and whether values are masked, come from the role's grants and branch scope; local UI state cannot add access to a report or column.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Roles and access decides, per role, which reports can be viewed, exported, emailed, scheduled or pulled by BI tools, at /admin/access.
Every screen, export, schedule, email request and API call checks these rules on the server, not just this screen.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Select a role to review its permissions (features) and, below, its per-report grants (view/export/email/schedule/BI) and any branch or masking limits.
2. Use "New role"/"Create role" to add a role, and "Delete role" to remove one that is no longer needed.
3. Toggle the grants for each report against the selected role, then "Save access" to persist the change.
4. Review user counts per role before deleting one, since removing a role removes those grants from every user holding it.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Administrators always have every permission and every report, so that grant set cannot be edited away.
Saving an invalid combination (for example a grant with no matching report) is rejected before the change is applied.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: This page itself is limited to administrators; the grants it edits are the same ones every other page in the module enforces.

The newest 500 matching entries are shown.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Use the search box (email, report id or detail) and the Area filter, then "Filter" to narrow the log; the query is kept in the URL so a filtered view can be reopened.
2. Review each entry's timestamp, actor, action, target and detail.
3. Clear the filters to return to the newest 500 entries overall.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A filter that matches nothing shows "No entries match." rather than an empty table with no explanation.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The email outbox records every email the system tried to send, with its delivery result, at /admin/outbox.

Every mail action in this reference demo is synthetic: an SMTP setting alone does not connect an actual mail provider, and no message leaves the system from this demo. Every attempted send is still recorded here so its content and recipients can be checked.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Review each message's status badge, subject and recipients.
2. Expand a message to see its full text and, when present, its error and attachments (with file size).

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A failed send shows its server-reported error inline in the expanded message.

A table of report-specific overrides follows for reports that set their own tighter on-screen limits, usually because they return one row per record.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Review and adjust organisation defaults (timezone, SMTP delivery) and the global on-screen row/period limits.
2. Use "Save settings"/"Save changes" to persist changes; they apply to every report, schedule and API pull after saving.
3. Review the report-specific limits table for reports with a tighter longest-period or most-rows override than the global default.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Requests above the configured on-screen limits are not loaded in the browser; the viewer instead offers a background run that is emailed or saved to My reports.

SMTP settings here select a delivery mode for the synthetic outbox; configuring them does not connect an actual mail provider in this demo, and every attempted message is recorded in the outbox instead of being sent.

2. For a connected source, review its datasets: domain, field count, rows loaded and when each was last refreshed.

3. For a planned connector with no datasets yet, note that a production connector must implement the source adapter against a read replica or warehouse and register its datasets; credentials belong only in server-side configuration.

2. Select a user to change their assigned roles and branch scope.
3. Save the change; the new access applies on the user's next request, since scope changes invalidate previously cached data.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: API keys and BI gives dashboards and spreadsheets read-only access to the reports the issuing user is allowed to see, at /api-keys.
A key acts as its owner: the same reports, branches and masking apply as when that person signs in.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Review existing keys and the reports each may pull; use "Create key" to issue a new one (only shown when the role may create keys).
2. Copy the generated key immediately - "Copy this key now. It will not be shown again."

3. Connect a BI tool using the shown base URL and key, following the tool-specific note (for example Power BI/Excel via Get data, From Web, with an Authorization: Bearer header, or Tableau's Web Data Connector).
4. Use "Revoke"/"Revoke key" to disable a key immediately once it is no longer needed.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Only reports with the API/BI action granted to that role are ever listed as pullable by a key; a revoked key stops working immediately on its next request.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Key creation is limited to roles allowed to create API keys; a key can never see more reports, branches or unmasked columns than its owner's own role.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Report builder lists every custom report definition the signed-in user may see, and opens a builder for a new or existing one, at /builder.

Custom reports are built from approved datasets (for example revenue, claims or admissions); in this reference demo the dataset content is synthetic, and a production deployment is expected to connect its own approved read-only data source rather than a live transactional database.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. From the list, review each report's dataset, visibility (private, shared with roles, or everyone) and owner (administrators only see the owner column), then "Edit" or delete it.
2. Select "New report" to start one: choose a dataset, then add grouping, measures and calculated columns; a preview of the results is shown before saving.
3. Use "Add measure" and "Add calculated column" to extend the report, "Refresh preview" to re-run it against the current definition, and "Reset" to discard unsaved changes.
4. Set the report's visibility and, for shared reports, the roles allowed to see it, then save; existing saved views and schedules that reference the report keep working after an edit.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: Saving validates the definition against the selected dataset; an invalid grouping, measure or calculated column is rejected with the specific error before the save completes.
Deleting a definition asks for confirmation naming the report; access, branch limits and masking continue to apply to anyone the report is shared with.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: Only roles with report-build access see "New report"/"Edit"; the owner column and cross-user visibility are limited to administrators.
Shared/everyone visibility does not bypass a viewer's own report, branch or column-masking grants.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Dashboards combine several reports on one page sharing a single period, at /dashboards.
Each widget still enforces the viewer's own report access and masking, even inside a shared dashboard.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: 1. Browse the dashboard tiles, each showing its name, visibility badge (Private, Shared or Everyone) and widget/owner summary; select a tile to open it.
2. Use "New dashboard" (only shown when the role may create dashboards) to start one; it opens private and empty.
3. Inside a dashboard, use "Edit" then "Add widget" to attach reports, and "Save dashboard" to persist the layout; "Delete dashboard" removes it entirely.
4. Use the sharing controls to change visibility and, for shared dashboards, the roles who may view it.

sections.title: Validation and recovery
paragraphs: A widget backed by a report the current viewer cannot access is not shown to that viewer, even though it may be visible to others on a shared dashboard.
Deleting a dashboard asks for confirmation before removing it for every viewer it was shared with.

sections.title: Access and preferences
paragraphs: New-dashboard and edit/delete controls are limited to roles allowed to build dashboards; every widget still checks the viewer's own report, branch and masking grants.
